抗甲狀腺藥物 甲狀腺活性和激素效應的降低可透過以下方式實現：干擾甲狀腺激素生成的藥物、修改甲狀腺激素組織反應的藥物，或透過放射或手術破壞腺體。Goitrogens 是抑制 T3 和 T4 分泌至低於正常水平的藥物，從而增加 TSH，進而導致腺體增大（甲狀腺腫）。臨床上使用的抗甲狀腺化合物包括 thioamides、iodides 和 radioactive iodine。
硫醯胺類 (THIOAMIDES) Thioamides 包括 methimazole 和 propylthiouracil，是治療甲狀腺機能亢進的主要藥物。在英國，carbimazole（體內轉換為 methimazole）被廣泛使用。Methimazole 的效力約為 propylthiouracil 的十倍，是成人和兒童的首選藥物。由於關於嚴重肝炎的黑框警告，propylthiouracil 應保留用於懷孕前三個月、甲狀腺風暴以及對 methimazole 產生不良反應（肝炎或顆粒球減少症除外）的患者。這些化合物的化學結構如圖 38-5 所示。Thiocarbamide 基團對抗甲狀腺活性至關重要。
藥物動力學 Methimazole 被完全吸收但吸收速率各異。它容易被甲狀腺蓄積，分布體積與 propylthiouracil 相似。排泄比 propylthiouracil 慢；48 小時內約 65-70% 的劑量在尿液中回收。
相反，propylthiouracil 被快速吸收，在 1 小時後達到血清峰值濃度。50-80% 的生體可用率可能是由於吸收不完全或肝臟首渡效應大。分布體積約等於全身水量，在甲狀腺蓄積。攝入的 propylthiouracil 大部分在 24 小時內以非活性葡萄糖醛酸苷形式由腎臟排泄。
這些藥物的血漿半衰期短（propylthiouracil 為 1.5 小時，methimazole 為 6 小時），但對抗甲狀腺作用或給藥間隔的持續時間影響不大，因為這兩種藥物都被甲狀腺蓄積。對於 propylthiouracil，每 6-8 小時給藥一次是合理的，因為單次 100 mg 劑量可抑制碘有機化 60% 長達 7 小時。由於單次 30 mg 劑量的 methimazole 可發揮超過 24 小時的抗甲狀腺作用，每日一次給藥對輕度至重度甲狀腺機能亢進的治療有效。
兩種 thioamides 都能穿過胎盤並被胎兒甲狀腺濃縮，因此在懷孕期間使用這些藥物必須謹慎。由於胎兒甲狀腺機能低下的風險，兩種 thioamides 被列為 FDA 懷孕分級 D（基於人類胎兒風險的證據，根據不良反應數據，見第 59 章）。兩者之中，propylthiouracil 在懷孕前三個月的使用較佳，因為它與蛋白質結合更強，因此較不容易穿過胎盤。此外，methimazole 雖罕見但已被報導與先天性畸形有關。兩種 thioamides 都以低濃度分泌到母乳中，但被認為對哺乳嬰兒安全。
藥效動力學 Thioamides 透過多重機制發揮作用。主要作用是透過抑制甲狀腺 peroxidase 催化的反應和阻斷 iodide 有機化來防止激素合成。此外，它們還阻斷 iodotyrosines 的耦合。它們不阻斷腺體對 iodide 的攝取。Propylthiouracil 和（程度小得多）methimazole 抑制 T4 和 T3 的週邊脫碘作用（圖 38-1）。由於影響的是激素的合成而非釋放，這些藥物的起始作用緩慢，通常需要 3-4 週才能耗盡 T4 的儲存。
毒性 Thioamides 的不良反應發生在 3-12% 的治療患者中。多數反應發生在早期，尤其是噁心和胃腸道不適。Methimazole 可能發生味覺或嗅覺改變。最常見的不良反應是斑丘疹性瘙癢皮疹（4-6%），有時伴隨發燒等全身徵象。罕見不良反應包括蕁麻疹性皮疹、血管炎、類狼瘡反應、淋巴結病變、低凝血酶原血症、剝脫性皮炎、多漿膜炎和急性關節痛。Propylthiouracil 已有嚴重肝炎（有时导致死亡）的報告（黑框警告），因此應避免用於兒童和成人，除非沒有其他選擇。膽汁淤積性黃疸在 methimazole 比 propylthiouracil 更常見。無症狀的轉氨酶升高也可能發生。
最危險的併發症是顆粒球減少症（顆粒球計數 < 500 cells/mm³），是一種不常見但可能致命的不良反應。它發生在 0.1-0.5% 服用 thioamides 的患者中，但老年患者和接受超過 40 mg/d methimazole 的患者風險可能增加。反應通常在停藥後迅速可逆，但可能需要廣效抗生素治療併發感染。顆粒球群落刺激因子（如 G-CSF；見第 33 章）可能加速顆粒球的恢復。Propylthiouracil 和 methimazole 之間的交叉過敏約為 50%；因此，不建議在有嚴重反應的患者中更換藥物。

陰離子抑制劑 (ANION INHIBITORS) Perchlorate (ClO4-)、pertechnetate (TcO4-) 和 thiocyanate (SCN-) 等單價陰離子可透過競爭性抑制 iodide 轉運機制來阻斷腺體對 iodide 的攝取。由於這些作用可被大劑量 iodides 克服，其效果有些不可預測。
Potassium perchlorate 的主要臨床用途是阻斷甲狀腺對 I- 的再攝取，用於 iodide 誘發的甲狀腺機能亢進患者（如 amiodarone 誘發的甲狀腺機能亢進）。然而，potassium perchlorate 臨床上很少使用，因為它與再生不良性貧血有關。
碘化物 (IODIDES) 在 1940 年代 thioamides 引入之前，iodides 是主要的抗甲狀腺藥物；如今它們很少作為單一療法使用。
藥效動力學 Iodides 對甲狀腺有多種作用。它們抑制有機化和激素釋放，並減小增生腺體的大小和血管分布。在易感個體中，iodides 可誘發甲狀腺機能亢進（Jod-Basedow 現象）或誘發甲狀腺機能低下。
在藥理劑量（> 6 mg/d）時，iodides 的主要作用是抑制激素釋放，可能是透過抑制甲狀腺球蛋白水解。甲狀腺毒性症狀的改善快速發生——在 2-7 天內——這是 iodide 治療甲狀腺風暴的價值所在。此外，iodides 降低增生腺體的血管分布、大小和脆性，使這些藥物成為手術前準備的宝贵药物。
Iodide 的臨床使用 Iodide 治療的缺點包括甲狀腺內碘儲存的增加，這可能延遲 thioamide 治療的起始或阻止放射性碘治療數週。因此，iodides 應在 thioamide 治療開始後才起始，並且如果可能使用放射性碘治療則應避免。Iodide 不應單獨使用，因為腺體會在 2-8 週內逃離 iodide 阻斷，而其停藥可能在富含碘的腺體中引起甲狀腺毒症的嚴重惡化。懷孕期間應避免慢性使用 iodides，因為它們穿過胎盤並可引起胎兒甲狀腺腫。在涉及放射性碘同位素釋放的放射緊急情況中，如果在接受輻射暴露前給予，potassium iodide 的甲狀腺阻斷效應可以保護腺體免受後續損傷。
毒性 對碘的不良反應（iodism）不常見，在大多數情況下停藥後可逆。它們包括痤瘡樣皮疹（類似 bromism）、唾液腺腫大、黏膜潰瘍、結膜炎、流鼻水、藥物熱、金屬味、出血性疾病，罕見有過敏性反應。
放射性碘 (RADIOACTIVE IODINE) 131I 是唯一用於治療甲狀腺毒症（其他用於診斷）的同位素。口服作為 sodium 131I 溶液給藥，它被快速吸收，被甲狀腺濃縮，並摻入儲存濾泡中。其治療效果取決於 β 射線的發射，有效半衰期為 5 天，穿透範圍為 400-2000 μm。在給藥後數週，甲狀腺實質的破壞表現為上皮水腫和壞死、濾泡破裂、水腫和白細胞浸潤。Radioiodine 的優點包括易於給予、有效、低成本和無痛。對放射性碘誘發遺傳損傷、白血病和腫瘤的擔憂，在放射性碘治療甲狀腺機能亢進超過 50 年的臨床經驗中並未實現。Radioactive iodine 不應給予孕婦或哺乳期母親，因為它穿過胎盤破壞胎兒甲狀腺，並在母乳中排泄。
腎上腺素受體阻斷劑 (ADRENOCEPTOR-BLOCKING AGENTS) 沒有內在擬交感活性的 β blockers（如 metoprolol、propranolol、atenolol）是甲狀腺毒症管理的有效治療輔助藥物，因為這些症狀中有許多類似交感神經刺激相關的症狀。Propranolol 是甲狀腺毒症治療中最廣泛使用的 β blocker。Beta blockers 可使甲狀腺機能亢進症狀臨床改善，但通常不會改變甲狀腺激素水平。劑量大於 160 mg/d 的 propranolol 也可能透過抑制 T4 到 T3 的週邊轉換使 T3 水平降低約 20%。

summary:
章節導讀

本章節介紹甲狀腺與抗甲狀腺藥物。

甲狀腺激素

  • T4（甲狀腺素）和 T3（三碘甲狀腺素）的合成需要碘和甲狀腺球蛋白
  • 脫碘酶將 T4 轉換為活性 T3 或無活性 reverse T3
  • 甲狀腺激素調節基礎代謝、促進生長發育

甲狀腺機能亢進治療

  • Thionamides（硫醯胺類）：Propylthiouracil（PTU）、Methimazole，抑制甲狀腺激素合成
  • Radioactive iodine (I-131)：破壞甲狀腺組織
  • Iodide：術前準備或甲狀腺風暴時短期使用

甲狀腺機能低下：Levothyroxine（左旋甲狀腺素）為首選治療

甲狀腺風暴：需緊急處理，包括 PTU、Iodide、Hydrocortisone、Propranolol

Introduction

甲狀腺激素的週邊代謝

甲狀腺激素週邊代謝的主要途徑是脫碘作用。T4 的脫碘作用可發生在 outer ring 的單脫碘作用，產生 3,5,3’-triiodothyronine (T3)，其效力是 T4 的三到四倍。或者，脫碘作用也可發生在 inner ring，產生 3,3’,5’-triiodothyronine (reverse T3，即 rT3)，此為無代謝活性（圖 38-2）。Amiodarone、含碘對比劑、β blockers 和皮質類固醇等藥物，以及嚴重疾病或飢餓狀態會抑制 T4 轉換為 T3 所需的 5’-deiodinase，導致血清中 T3 降低而 rT3 升高。甲狀腺激素的藥物動力學列於表 38-1。正常個體血清中 T3 和 rT3 濃度低，是由於這兩種化合物的高代謝清除率所致。

甲狀腺功能的評估

用於評估甲狀腺功能的檢驗列於表 38-2。

A. 甲狀腺─腦下垂體關係

甲狀腺功能透過甲狀腺─腦下垂體回饋控制，在第 37 章也有討論。簡而言之，下視丘細胞分泌 thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH)（圖 38-3）。TRH 被分泌到腦下垂體���脈系統的毛細血管中，在腦下垂體中，TRH 刺激甲狀腺刺激素（甲狀腺刺激激素，TSH）的合成與釋放。TSH 接著刺激甲狀腺細胞中的 adenylyl cyclase 媒介機制，以增加 T4 和 T3 的合成與釋放。這些甲狀腺激素以負回饋方式作用於下視丘和腦下垂體以控制甲狀腺功能。
title: 甲狀腺與抗甲狀腺藥物

CH52 癌症化學治療 章節導讀 癌症化學治療（化療）是惡性腫瘤治療的重要支柱之一。本章節系統介紹細胞週期動力學基礎、藥物作用機轉分類（細胞週期特異性與非特異性藥物）、藥物合併治療原則、抗藥性機轉，以及各類化療藥物的藥理學特性。化療的成功有賴於正確的藥物選擇、劑量強度管理及對不良反應的及時處理。
細胞週期動力學基礎 細胞週期各時期 時期 主要事件 化療藥物作用點 G₀期（靜止期） 細胞處於休眠狀態，不進行分裂 CCNS藥物可作用 G₁期（DNA合成前期） 細胞準備DNA合成 主要由CCNS藥物殺滅 S期（DNA合成期） DNA複製；放射菌素D、6-MP等 CCS藥物主要作用點 G₂期（DNA合成後期） 準備有絲分裂 博萊黴素、紫杉醇等 M期（有絲分裂期） 細胞分裂 長春花生物鹼、紫杉醇 對數殺滅假說（Log-Kill Hypothesis） 核心概念：化療藥物在治療劑量範圍內，按固定比例殺滅腫瘤細胞，而非固定數量。
例如：某藥物可將腫瘤細胞數從10¹⁰降至10⁷（3 log殺滅），同樣劑量可將10⁵降至10²。這意味著腫瘤越小，達到治愈所需的化療週期越少。
化療藥物分類 細胞週期特異性藥物（CCS） 類別 代表藥物 作用時期 抗代謝藥物 5-FU、MTX、6-MP、gemcitabine、capecitabine S期 長春花生物鹼 Vinblastine、Vincristine、Vinorelbine M期 紫杉醇類 Paclitaxel、Docetaxel M期 喜樹鹼類 Irinotecan、Topotecan S期（topoisomerase I抑制） 細胞週期非特異性藥物（CCNS） 類別 代表藥物 烷化劑 Cyclophosphamide、melphalan、chlorambucil、nitrosoureas 鉑類製劑 Cisplatin、carboplatin、oxaliplatin 抗腫瘤抗生素 Doxorubicin、daunorubicin、bleomycin Epipodophyllotoxins Etoposide（topoisomerase II抑制） 藥物合併治療原則 有效的化療組合需滿足以下原則：
原則 說明 有效性 只選擇對特定腫瘤單獨使用時有效的藥物 毒性互補 各藥物的劑量限制毒性不重疊（如A骨髓抑制、B腎毒性） 最佳時程 藥物應按其最佳給藥時程給予 作用機轉互補 不同生化機轉的藥物合併可減少抗藥性產生 劑量強度與治療失敗 **劑量強度（dose intensity）**是化療成功的關鍵限制因素之一。
動物實驗顯示：劑量-反應曲線在線性階段非常陡峭 降低劑量20%即可導致治療失敗 增加給藥間隔會減少劑量強度，降低療效 抗藥性機轉 抗藥性類型 機轉 內因性抗藥 腫瘤從未對藥物有過反應（如黑色素瘤、腎細胞癌、腦癌） 獲得性抗藥 暴露於藥物後產生；可分為： — 單一藥物特異性 由特定基因改變引起 — 多重抗藥性（MDR） MDR1基因增幅；P-glycoprotein增加導致藥物外流；對結構無關的藥物（anthracyclines、vinca alkaloids、taxanes等）均具抗藥性 烷化劑（Alkylating Agents） 作用機轉：將烷基轉移至DNA的鳥糞嘌呤N7位置，造成DNA鏈間或鏈內交聯，阻止DNA複製與轉錄。
臨床常用製劑 藥物 主要適應症 劑量限制毒性 Cyclophosphamide 淋巴瘤、乳癌、卵巢癌 出血性膀胱炎、骨髓抑制 Ifosfamide 軟組織肉瘤、睪丸癌 出血性膀胱炎（需同時給予mesna） Melphalan 多發性骨髓瘤 骨髓抑制 Cisplatin 睪丸癌、卵巢癌、肺癌 腎毒性、周邊神經病變、聽力損失 Carboplatin 卵巢癌、肺癌 骨髓抑制（血小板減少為主） Oxaliplatin 大腸直腸癌 週邊感覺神經病變（累積性） 常見不良反應 系統 表現 骨髓 劑量限制性骨髓抑制（嗜中性球、血小板減少） 胃腸道 噁心、嘔吐（可用5-HT₃拮抗劑+dexamethasone預防） 生殖 不孕症（卵巢/睪丸功能抑制） 致突變/致癌 治療後可能發生二次白血病 抗代謝藥物（Antimetabolites） 作用機轉：結構類似正常代謝物，干擾核酸合成或蛋白質修飾。
常用藥物 藥物 作用機轉 主要適應症 Methotrexate (MTX) 抑制二氫葉酸還原酶（DHFR） 絨毛膜癌、白血病、淋巴瘤、乳癌 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) 抑制胸苷酸合成酶（TS） 大腸直腸癌、乳癌 Capecitabine 口服前藥，轉化為5-FU 大腸直腸癌、乳癌 Gemcitabine 抑制DNA合成酶 胰臟癌、肺癌、膀胱癌 6-Mercaptopurine (6-MP) 抑制嘌呤合成 急性淋巴性白血病 Methotrexate 毒性與解毒 大劑量MTX治療需同時給予leucovorin（folinic acid）救援，以保護正常細胞。
毒性 說明 骨髓抑制 劑量限制性 腎毒性 MTX結晶沉積於腎小管 肝毒性 長期使用導致肝纖維化 肺毒性 過敏性肺炎 抗腫瘤抗生素（Antitumor Antibiotics） 藥物 作用機轉 主要適應症 特殊毒性 Doxorubicin 嵌入DNA；topoisomerase II抑制 乳癌、淋巴瘤、肉瘤 心臟毒性（累積性心肌病變）；最大累積劑量550 mg/m² Daunorubicin 同上 急性骨髓性白血病 心臟毒性 Bleomycin 產生自由基，斷裂DNA 淋巴瘤、睪丸癌 肺纖維化（劑量限制性）；發燒過敏 Mitomycin C 烷化作用 胃腸道癌症、膀胱癌 骨髓抑制（延遲性） 植物生物鹼（Plant Alkaloids） 長春花生物鹼（Vinca Alkaloids） 作用機轉：與β-tubulin結合，抑制微小管組裝，阻止有絲分裂紡錘體形成。
藥物 主要適應症 主要毒性 Vincristine 急性淋巴性白血病、淋巴瘤 神經毒性（週邊感覺異常、便秘） Vinblastine 睪丸癌、淋巴瘤 骨髓抑制 Vinorelbine 肺癌、乳癌 骨髓抑制 紫杉醇類（Taxanes） 作用機轉：促進微小管聚合並抑制其解聚，阻止紡錘體功能，將細胞阻斷於G₂/M期。
藥物 主要適應症 主要毒性 Paclitaxel 卵巢癌、乳癌、肺癌 過敏反應（需預防性給予類固醇+抗組織胺）；骨髓抑制 Docetaxel 乳癌、肺癌、前列腺癌 液體滯留症候群；指甲病變 喜樹鹼類（Camptothecins） 作用機轉：抑制topoisomerase I，阻止DNA複製過程中的超螺旋修復。
藥物 主要適應症 主要毒性 Irinotecan 大腸直腸癌（與5-FU+leucovorin合併） 延遲性腹瀉；骨髓抑制 Topotecan 卵巢癌、小細胞肺癌 骨髓抑制 激素製劑（Hormonal Agents） 特點：對荷爾蒙依賴性腫瘤有效；作用機轉為抑制激素合成或阻斷激素受體。
藥物 機轉 主要適應症 主要不良反應 Tamoxifen 選擇性雌激素受體調節劑（SERM） 乳癌 子宮內膜癌風險；熱潮紅 Anastrozole/Letrozole 芳香酶抑制劑 停經後乳癌 骨質疏鬆 Flutamide/Bicalutamide 雄性素受體拮抗劑 前列腺癌 肝毒性 Dexamethasone 糖皮質素 淋巴瘤、白血病（腦部浸潤） 免疫抑制 標靶治療藥物（Targeted Therapy） 單株抗體 藥物 標的 主要適應症 Rituximab CD20（B細胞） B細胞淋巴瘤 Trastuzumab HER2 HER2+乳癌 Cetuximab EGFR 大腸直腸癌、頭頸癌 Bevacizumab VEGF 大腸直腸癌、肺癌 小分子抑制劑 藥物 標的 主要適應症 Imatinib BCR-ABL, c-KIT 慢性骨髓性白血病（CML）、GIST Gefitinib/Erlotinib EGFR 肺癌（EGFR突變型） Sunitinib 多重受體酪胺酸激酶 腎細胞癌、GIST 化療輔助治療 止嘔藥物（CNE prophylaxis） 層級 藥物組合 適用情境 高致嘔風險 5-HT₃拮抗劑 + Dexamethasone + NK₁受體拮抗劑（aprepitant） Cisplatin ≥70 mg/m² 中致嘔風險 5-HT₃拮抗劑 + Dexamethasone Carboplatin、anthracycline+cyclophosphamide 低致嘔風險 Dexamethasone alone 5-FU、MTX 造血生長因子 製劑 適應症 Filgrastim (G-CSF) 預防嗜中性球減少性發燒 Epoetin alfa (EPO) 化療相關貧血 化療藥物不良反應快速參考 系統 常見元兇藥物 處理要點 骨髓抑制 大多數化療藥物 監測血球計數；必要時输血、G-CSF支持 噁心/嘔吐 Cisplatin、anthracyclines 5-HT₃拮抗劑+類固醇為主 心臟毒性 Doxorubicin 累積劑量限制；心臟超聲監測 肺毒性 Bleomycin 最大累積劑量400單位；監測肺功能 腎毒性 Cisplatin、MTX 充分水化；必要時鹼化尿液 神經毒性 Vincristine、Oxaliplatin 無特殊解藥；劑量調整 出血性膀胱炎 Cyclophosphamide、Ifosfamide Mesna預防；充分水化 脫髮 Anthracyclines、taxanes 衛教；考慮降低頭部溫度（cold cap）

CH59 皮膚藥理學 章節導讀 皮膚疾病提供了一個獨特的藥物給藥途徑——局部給藥。本章節介紹皮膚藥理學的基本原理，包括藥物經皮吸收的因素、皮膚局部用藥的 Vehicles（載體）選擇，以及常用皮膚藥物的藥理學特性。涵蓋抗菌、抗黴菌、抗病毒藥物以及常用於皮膚疾病的皮質類固醇、Retinoids等藥物。
經皮吸收的基本原理 影響藥物穿透皮膚的因素 因素 說明 身體部位 陰囊、面部、腋下、头皮渗透性最高；前臂最低 濃度梯度 濃度越高，單位時間穿透量越大 給藥頻次 皮膚作為儲庫；很多藥物可每日一次 Vehicles 不同載體影響蒸發速率及藥物釋放 皮膚完整性 受损皮膚吸收顯著增加 Vehicles（載體）選擇原則 急性炎症（有滲出） 慢性炎症（乾燥、鱗屑） 酊劑、濕敷、懸浮劑 乳霜、軟膏 載體類型 特性 軟膏（Ointment） 最保濕；油脂性；適於乾燥、鱗屑病變 乳霜（Cream） 保濕但較不油膩；適於一般用途 懸浮劑（Lotion） 蒸發後留薄層藥物；適於毛髮區域 凝胶（Gel） 水性基底；較不油膩 泡沫（Foam） 毛髮區域方便使用 局部抗菌藥物 Bacitracin與Gramicidin 特性 說明 抗菌譜 格蘭氏陽性菌（葡萄球菌、鏈球菌、肺炎球菌） 常用製劑 與neomycin、polymyxin B合併（三抗菌軟膏） 不良反應 過敏性接觸性皮膚炎；系統吸收極微 Mupirocin（莫匹羅星） 作用機轉：結構獨特的抗生素，抑制細菌蛋白質合成。
特性 說明 抗菌譜 格蘭氏陽性菌，包括MSSA、MRSA、A群β溶血性鏈球菌 適應症 膿痂疹（S. aureus、A群鏈球菌）；微創傷繼發感染 給藥 局部軟膏；每日2-3次 Retapamulin 作用機轉：Pleromutilin衍生物，抑制細菌蛋白質合成。
特性 說明 抗菌譜 A群β溶血性鏈球菌、S. aureus（不含MRSA） 適應症 非複雜性膿痂疹；9個月以上兒童及成人 療程 每日2次×5天 Polymyxin B 抗菌譜：格蘭氏陰性菌（Pseudomonas aeruginosa、E. coli、Klebsiella）
注意：總劑量不超過200 mg/日（開放性傷口或燒傷面積大時系統吸收增加）
Neomycin與Gentamicin 藥物 抗菌譜 Neomycin 格蘭氏陰性菌（E. coli、Proteus、Klebsiella）；對Pseudomonas效果差 Gentamicin 對Pseudomonas效果較neomycin佳；對格蘭氏陽性菌也有活性 不良反應：過敏性接觸性皮膚炎常見；大面積使用可能導致腎毒性/耳毒性
青春痘（Acne）的局部抗生素治療 Clindamycin 作用機轉：抑制Propionibacterium acnes；體外抗菌活性
製劑 說明 1%凝膠、乳液、溶液 每日1-2次 固定複方製劑 clindamycin + benzoyl peroxide（Acanya, Duac） Erythromycin 特點：游離鹼基而非鹽類製劑；渗透性較佳
不良反應：用於治療青春痘時可能出現刺激性；過敏性接觸性皮膚炎少見
其他青春痘局部用藥 藥物 作用/適應症 不良反應 Azelaic acid 抗菌、抗發炎；輕-中度青春痘 輕微刺激 Dapsone 5% gel 抗發炎；青春痘 輕微乾燥、紅斑 Benzoyl peroxide 抗菌；與clindamycin合用效果佳 乾燥、脫皮 局部抗黴菌藥物 黴菌感染分類 病原 感染的皮膚病變 Epidermophyton、Microsporum、Trichophyton 皮癬菌感染（足癬、股癬、體癬） Candida albicans 念珠菌感染（間擦疹、口腔鵝口瘡） Malassezia furfur 花斑癬（tinea versicolor） Imidazoles類（局部抗黴菌） 藥物 適應症 Clotrimazole 皮癬菌、念珠菌； OTC Miconazole 皮癬菌、念珠菌；也有靜脈製劑用於全身黴菌病 Ketoconazole 皮癬菌、念珠菌；也有口服製劑 Econazole、Sulconazole 皮癬菌、念珠菌 作用機轉：抑制黴菌細胞膜的ergosterol合成（阻斷lanosterol 14α-demethylase）
Allylamines類 藥物 特點 Terbinafine 對皮癬菌高效；也有口服製劑（用於甲癬） Naftifine 局部高效抗黴菌 作用機轉：抑制squalene epoxidase → 黴菌細胞膜ergosterol耗竭
劑量：2%乳膏；每日2次
口服抗黴菌藥物 Terbinafine（口服） 適應症 劑量 甲癬（onychomycosis） 250 mg/d×6週（指甲）；12週（腳趾甲） Ketoconazole（口服） ⚠️ 肝毒性顯著：需監測肝功能；建議用於嚴重黴菌感染
適應症 說明 慢性黏膜皮膚念珠菌病 200 mg/d；可能需長期維持 花斑癬 200 mg/d×5天 Griseofulvin（口服） 作用機轉：干擾黴菌細胞骨架形成；抑制有絲分裂
適應症 說明 皮癬菌感染 對头皮癬、股癬效果好；指甲/腳趾甲需長期治療（6-18個月） 不良反應：頭痛、噁心、光敏感；可能引起血紅素下降；禁用於porphyria患者
局部抗病毒藥物 Acyclovir 特性 說明 適應症 單純皰疹病毒（HSV-1, HSV-2）感染 5%軟膏 每日5次×5天 Penciclovir 特性 說明 適應症 唇部復發性單純皰疹 1%乳膏 每2小時一次×4天 皮質類固醇（局部） 效能分級 等級 藥物 說明 最強（Class I） Clobetasol propionate、Betamethasone dipropionate 極強效；只用於嚴重、頑固性病變；禁長期大面積使用 強效（Class II-III） Fluocinonide、Mometasone furoate 中-強效；通常不超過2週 弱效（Class IV-V） Hydrocortisone、Desonide 輕-中效；兒童及臉部首選 常見不良反應（長期使用） 系統 表現 皮膚萎縮 皮膚變薄、皮紋、脆弱 紫斑 血管脆弱 類固醇痤瘡 毛囊炎 毛細血管擴張 泛血絲 接觸過敏 對製劑中其他成分過敏 Retinoids（維生素A衍生物） 局部Tretinoin（維A酸） 作用機轉：穩定溶酶體；增加RNA polymerase活性；促進表皮細胞更新；減少毛孔阻塞
適應症 說明 青春痘 輕-中度；首選之一 光老化 長期使用促進膠原蛋白新生；減少皺紋 口服Isotretinoin ⚠️ 嚴重青春痘（囊腫型）的首選治療
特性 說明 作用機轉 抑制皮脂分泌；減少P. acnes；抗發炎 療程 0.5-1 mg/kg/d×4-6個月；通常總劑量120-150 mg/kg 不良反應 口唇乾燥脫皮；血脂肪升高；肝功能異常；致畸性 ⚠️ 致畸性極強：生育年齡女性必需使用兩種避孕方法；iPLEDGE計畫强制登記
驅蟲藥物（局部用於疥瘡） Permethrin（氯菊酯） 特性 說明 適應症 疥瘡；頭蝨 5%乳膏 頭蝨：塗抹全頭並保留10分鐘後沖洗；疥瘡：頸部以下塗抹，保留8-14小時 不良反應 短暫燒灼感、刺痛 Lindane（林丹） ⚠️ 神經毒性風險：可能抑制中樞神經系統；早產兒、癲癇患者禁用；加州禁用
皮膚美白劑 Hydroquinone（氫醌） 作用機轉：抑制tyrosinase → 減少黑色素合成
特性 說明 濃度 2-4%乳膏 適應症 黑斑、雀斑 不良反應 刺激；過敏性接觸性皮膚炎；外源性褐黃病（過度使用時） 防曬劑（Sunscreens） 防曬係數（SPF） SPF = 有防曬劑時的最小紅斑劑量 / 無防曬劑時的最小紅斑劑量
SPF值 防護效果 SPF 15 阻擋約93% UVB SPF 30 阻擋約97% UVB SPF 50+ 阻擋約98% UVB 寬頻防護（Broad Spectrum）：同時防護UVA與UVB
常用防曬成分 類別 代表藥物 防護範圍 PABA酯 Padimate O UVB 苯甲酮 Oxybenzone UVB/部分UVA 二苯甲酮 Avobenzone (Parsol 1789) UVA 二氧化鈦 Titanium dioxide 物理性遮蔽；广譜
summary:
CH59 皮膚藥理學

章節導讀

皮膚疾病提供了一個獨特的藥物給藥途徑——局部給藥。本章節介紹皮膚藥理學的基本原理，包括藥物經皮吸收的因素、皮膚局部用藥的 Vehicles（載體）選擇，以及常用皮膚藥物的藥理學特性。涵蓋抗菌、抗黴菌、抗病毒藥物以及常用於皮膚疾病的皮質類固醇、Retinoids等藥物。

經皮吸收的基本原理

影響藥物穿透皮膚的因素

因素 說明
身體部位 陰囊、面部、腋下、头皮渗透性最高；前臂最低
濃度梯度 濃度越高，單位時間穿透量越大
給藥頻次 皮膚作為儲庫；很多藥物可每日一次
Vehicles 不同載體影響蒸發速率及藥物釋放
皮膚完整性 受损皮膚吸收顯著增加

Vehicles（載體）選擇原則

急性炎症（有滲出） 慢性炎症（乾燥、鱗屑）
酊劑、濕敷、懸浮劑 乳霜、軟膏
載體類型 特性
軟膏（Ointment） 最保濕；油脂性；適於乾燥、鱗屑病變
乳霜（Cream） 保濕但較不油膩；適於一般用途
懸浮劑（Lotion） 蒸發後留薄層藥物；適於毛髮區域
凝胶（Gel） 水性基底；較不油膩
泡沫（Foam） 毛髮區域方便使用

局部抗菌藥物

Bacitracin與Gramicidin

特性 說明
抗菌譜 格蘭氏陽性菌（葡萄球菌、鏈球菌、肺炎球菌）
常用製劑 與neomycin、polymyxin B合併（三抗菌軟膏）
不良反應 過敏性接觸性皮膚炎；系統吸收極微

Mupirocin（莫匹羅星）

作用機轉：結構獨特的抗生素，抑制細菌蛋白質合成。

content:
CH60 眼科用藥 章節導讀 眼科用藥是臨床藥理學的重要分支，涉及局部（眼藥水、軟膏）與全身性藥物在眼部的應用。本章節介紹常用眼科藥物的藥理學特性，包括青光眼治療藥物（β-blockers、 prostaglandin analogues、碳酸酐酶抑制劑）、散瞳藥物、局部麻醉劑以及影響視力的全身性藥物（如amiodarone、ethambutol等）。眼科用藥需特別注意眼藥水的全身性吸收帶來的不良反應。
眼科用藥的基本原理 局部用藥的考量 因素 說明 全身性吸收 眼藥水可通過鼻淚管全身吸收；必要時壓迫內眼角（淚囊）以減少吸收 防腐劑 長期使用含benzalkonium chloride的眼藥水可能引起接觸性過敏 ** viscosity** 增加黏稠度可延長眼藥水在結膜囊的停留時間 青光眼藥物 青光眼治療概述 青光眼是由視神經退化導致的視野缺損疾病；眼內壓（IOP）升高是其主要危險因子。
青光眼藥物分類 藥物類別 代表藥物 作用機轉 β-blockers Timolol、Betaxolol、Carteolol 減少房水生成 Prostaglandin analogues Latanoprost、Bimatoprost、 Travoprost 增加葡萄膜鞏膜外流 α₂-agonists Brimonidine、Apraclonidine 減少房水生成；增加外流 碳酸酐酶抑制劑 Dorzolamide、Brinzolamide（局部） 減少碳酸氫鹽分泌→減少房水 膽鹼激動劑 Pilocarpine 收縮瞳孔→拉緊小梁網→增加外流 ** Rho激酶抑制劑** Netarsudil 增加小梁網外流 β-腎上腺素阻斷劑（局部） Timolol（馬來酸噻嗎洛爾） 作用機轉：非選擇性β-blocker；局部使用減少睫狀上皮細胞的房水生成。
特性 說明 濃度 0.25%, 0.5% 給藥 每日1-2次 療效 降低IOP約20-30% 不良反應（全身性吸收） ⚠️ 老年患者、心臟疾病患者、氣喘/COPD患者需特別注意
系統 表現 心臟 心搏過緩、心衰竭惡化、房室傳導阻斷 呼吸 氣喘/ COPD惡化 中樞神經 憂鬱、意識混淆、陽痿 局部 點狀角膜炎、眼睛刺激、視力模糊 β1-選擇性製劑 藥物 優點 Betaxolol 對心臟选择性較高；氣喘患者相对安全 Prostaglandin Analogues Latanoprost（拉坦前列素） 作用機轉：Prostaglandin F₂α衍生物；增加葡萄膜鞏膜外流通道的房水排出。
特性 說明 降低IOP幅度 約25-35% 給藥 每晚一次 優點 全身不良反應少；每日一次方便 不良反應 系統 表現 眼睛 眼睛發紅（結膜充血）、虹膜色素沉著增加（棕色眼睛變深）、睫毛增長變粗、眼皮色素沉著 全身 肌肉/關節疼痛；皮疹 注意：可能使睫毛、外眼周的毛髮變黑、變粗、變長
α₂-腎上腺素激動劑 Brimonidine（溴莫尼定） 作用機轉：α₂受體激動；減少房水生成並增加葡萄膜鞏膜外流。
特性 說明 降低IOP幅度 約20-25% 給藥 每日2-3次 不良反應 系統 表現 局部 過敏性結膜炎（約10-20%患者）、眼睛發紅、瘙癢 全身 口乾、嗜睡（α₂中枢作用） 碳酸酐酶抑制劑（局部） Dorzolamide（多佐胺） 作用機轉：抑制碳酸酐酶II → 減少睫狀上皮細胞分泌碳酸氫鹽 → 減少房水生成
特性 說明 製劑 2%眼藥水；每日3次 單獨使用療效 降低IOP約15-20% 注意：磺胺類過敏患者禁用（結構相關）
Brinzolamide（布林唑胺） 特點：與dorzolamide相似；pH較低，舒適度可能較佳
膽鹼激動劑（Pilocarpine，毛果芸香鹼） 作用機轉：直接作用的膽鹼酯酶抑制劑；收縮瞳孔（miosis）→拉緊小梁網→增加房水外流
特性 說明 濃度 1-4% 給藥 每日2-4次 降低IOP 約15-25% 不良反應 系統 表現 眼睛 瞳孔縮小（暗視力下降）、眉弓疼痛、視力模糊（晶狀體變凸） 全身 口腔發汗、唾液分泌過多；全身吸收可能引起心搏過緩 散瞳藥物（Mydriatics）與睫狀肌麻痺藥物（Cycloplegics） 藥物 作用 臨床用途 Tropicamide 快速散瞳（30-60分鐘）；短效睫狀肌麻痺 眼底檢查 Cyclopentolate 散瞳+睫狀肌麻痺（24-48小時） 驗光；葡萄膜炎 Homatropine 散瞳+睫狀肌麻痺（2-4天） 葡萄膜炎 Atropine 散瞳+睫狀肌麻痺（7-10天） 嚴重葡萄膜炎；兒童使用有窒息風險 作用機轉：抗膽鹼→阻斷虹膜括約肌（散瞳）和睫狀肌（睫狀肌麻痺）
局部麻醉劑 Proparacaine（Tetracaine） 作用機轉：抑制神經細胞的鈉離子通道→阻止動作電位產生
特性 說明 作用開始 數秒內 作用持續 10-20分鐘 用途 眼科操作（測量眼壓、移除異物、縫線拆除） 注意：長期使用可能延遲角膜癒合；不可用於治療眼睛疼痛
抗感染眼科製劑 局部抗生素 藥物 適應症 Erythromycin 0.5%軟膏 新生兒眼炎預防（Neisseria gonorrhoeae、Chlamydia trachomatis）；常規新生兒處理後 Gentamicin/ Tobramycin眼藥水 格蘭氏陰性菌感染（Pseudomonas） Ciprofloxacin/ Ofloxacin眼藥水 角膜潰痬；Fluoroquinolones穿透性佳 局部抗病毒藥物 藥物 適應症 Ganciclovir凝膠 皰疹性角膜炎 Trifluridine眼藥水 皰疹性角膜炎 抗發炎眼科藥物 皮質類固醇 藥物 用途 Prednisolone acetate 1% 葡萄膜炎；術後抗發炎 Dexamethasone眼藥水/軟膏 過敏性結膜炎；術後 ⚠️ 長期使用局部類固醇的風險：白內障（皮質類固醇性）；眼壓升高（類固醇性青光眼）；角膜融解（皰疹性角膜炎時使用可能加劇）
NSAIDs眼科製劑 藥物 用途 Ketorolac眼藥水 術後止痛；過敏性結膜炎瘙癢 Nepafenac眼藥水 白內障術後抗發炎 老化相關黃斑部病變（AMD）治療 抗血管內皮生長因子（Anti-VEGF）治療 藥物 給藥方式 說明 Ranibizumab 玻璃體內注射 非常昂貴 Bevacizumab 玻璃體內注射（仿單外使用） 較便宜 Aflibercept 玻璃體內注射 VEGF trap 適應症：濕型（新生血管型）老化相關黃斑部病變
全身性藥物的眼科不良反應 藥物 眼部不良反應 Amiodarone 角膜沉著物（前囊下）；視力模糊 Ethambutol 視神經炎→視力下降、紅綠色盲 Corticosteroids 白內障（後囊下）；眼壓升高（類固醇性青光眼） Tamoxifen 視網膜病變；角膜混濁 Vigabatrin 不可逆性視野缺損；使用時需監測視野 Phenytoin 眼球震顫（過量時） Ethambutol眼科監測：建議治療前及治療中每2-4週進行視野及色覺檢查
眼科用藥的使用技巧 技巧 說明 壓迫淚囊 點藥後輕壓內眼角2-3分鐘；減少全身吸收 等待時間 不同眼藥水間至少等待5分鐘 正確順序 水溶性→懸浮性→軟膏（最後） 開瓶後保存 多劑量眼藥水開瓶後一般保存28天（不含防腐劑者更短）
summary:
CH60 眼科用藥

章節導讀

眼科用藥是臨床藥理學的重要分支，涉及局部（眼藥水、軟膏）與全身性藥物在眼部的應用。本章節介紹常用眼科藥物的藥理學特性，包括青光眼治療藥物（β-blockers、 prostaglandin analogues、碳酸酐酶抑制劑）、散瞳藥物、局部麻醉劑以及影響視力的全身性藥物（如amiodarone、ethambutol等）。眼科用藥需特別注意眼藥水的全身性吸收帶來的不良反應。

眼科用藥的基本原理

局部用藥的考量

因素 說明

** viscosity** 增加黏稠度可延長眼藥水在結膜囊的停留時間

content:
章節導讀 本章介紹組織胺（H₁、H₂、H₃受體）與血清素（5-HT）受體的生理作用及相關藥物，並說明麥角生物鹼在偏頭痛治療與婦產科的應用。
組織胺（Histamine） 組織胺儲存於肥大細胞與嗜鹼性球中，過敏反應時釋放。
H₁受體效應 效應 說明 平滑肌收縮 支氣管、子宮、血管 血管通透性增加 導致水腫 癢感與疼痛 過敏反應常見 H₂受體效應 效應 說明 胃酸分泌增加 消化性潰疡主因 心率增加 正性頻率作用 抑制組織胺釋放 負回饋調節 H₃受體效應 中樞神經突觸前自體受體，抑制組織胺釋放 抗組織胺藥物 H₁阻斷劑 第一代H₁阻斷劑（Diphenhydramine、Chlorpheniramine）
可穿透血腦屏障（BBB） → 鎮靜 具有抗膽鹼效應 臨床用途：過敏、動暈症、失眠 第二代H₁阻斷劑（Loratadine、Cetirizine、Fexofenadine）

5-HT受體分類 受體 訊號途徑 主要功能 5-HT₁ Gi → 抑制腺苷酸環化酶 血管收縮、抑制釋放 5-HT₂ Gq → 增加IP₃/DAG 平滑肌收縮、血小板聚集 5-HT₃ 配體門控陽離子通道 嘔吐反射 5-HT₄ Gs → 刺激腺苷酸環化酶 平滑肌鬆弛 5-HT₇ Gs → 鬆弛平滑肌 血管擴張 相關藥物 藥物 機轉 臨床用途 Ondansetron 5-HT₃拮抗劑 化療/手術後噁心嘔吐 Sumatriptan 5-HT₁B/₁D激動劑 急性偏頭痛 SSRIs 增加突觸5-HT 憂鬱症 麥角生物鹼（Ergot Alkaloids） 麥角生物鹼由真菌Claviceps purpurea產生，對多個受體具有部分激動/拮抗活性。

content:
CH58 老年藥理學 章節導讀 老年人的藥理學特性與年輕成人有顯著差異，主要源於年齡相關的生理功能下降，包括腎功能減退、肝臟代謝能力改變、身體組成分變化及藥效學敏感度改變。本章節介紹老年人藥動學與藥效學的變化，以及主要藥物類別（心血管藥物、中樞神經藥物、抗感染藥物等）在老年人中的使用原則與不良反應風險。
老年人生理變化與藥動學 腎功能減退 腎絲球濾過率（GFR）随年齡下降，約2/3老年人有此現象。
問題 說明 血清肌酸酐的誤導性 老年人的肌肉量減少，肌酸酐產生減少；即使腎功能已下降，血清肌酸酐可能仍在正常範圍 Cockcroft-Gault公式 適用於40-80歲：CrCl = [(140-年齡)×體重(kg)] / [72×血清肌酸酐(mg/dL)]；女性×0.85 臨床意義：主要經腎臟排除的藥物（如aminoglycosides、digoxin、lithium、部分penicillins）需根據腎功能調整劑量。
肝臟代謝能力變化 變化 說明 肝臟血流減少 60-80歲約為年輕人的55-60% CYP450酶活性 Phase I反應（氧化）下降；Phase II反應（接合）變化較小 肝臟恢復能力 肝炎或肝毒性物質損傷後恢復能力下降 肝臟清除減少的藥物 肝臟清除不變的藥物 Diazepam、Alprazolam Lorazepam、Oxazepam Meperidine、Nortriptyline Lidocaine、Prazosin Propranolol、Theophylline Warfarin、Isoniazid 身體組成分變化 變化 說明 體水分減少 61%（年輕成人）→ 53%（老年人）；水溶性藥物分佈體積減少 體脂肪增加 脂溶性藥物（如benzodiazepines、anesthetics）分佈體積增加，半衰期延長 肌肉量減少 影響digoxin等藥物的分佈 白蛋白減少 游離藥物比例增加；影響高度蛋白質結合藥物 老年人的藥效學變化 中樞神經系統藥物敏感性增加 老年人對多種中樞神經藥物更敏感，包括：
藥物類別 敏感性增加的表現 Benzodiazepines 嗜睡、共濟失調；跌倒風險增加 Opioids 呼吸抑制作用增強 Antipsychotics 錐體外症狀增加 Antidepressants 抗膽鹼作用更明顯 心血管系統的代償機制減退 變化 說明 心輸出量對運動的反應減退 心搏過速減少，依賴增加每搏輸出量 姿勢性低血壓 姿勢改變時血壓調節能力下降；跌倒風險 體溫調節受損 對體溫過高或過低更敏感 主要藥物類別在老年人中的使用 心血管藥物 抗高血壓藥物 藥物類別 老年人使用要點 Thiazide利尿劑 首選之一；但低劑量使用（避免低血鉀、高血糖、高尿酸） Ca channel blockers 有效；注意便秘（diltiazem/verapamil）和水腫（dihydropyridines） β-blockers 對老年人較β-blockers效果差（老年人β受體反應下降）；阻塞性肺疾病者禁用 ACE抑制劑/ARB 對心衰竭、糖尿病者有腎臟保護作用；但老年人起始劑量要低 注意：老年人使用任何抗高血壓藥物都應定期監測姿勢性低血壓。
毛地黃（Digoxin） 特性 說明 腎排泄 半衰期延長（> 50%老年人） 毒性風險增加 心律不整、噁心、精神障礙 劑量建議 維持劑量通常需降低；監測血清濃度 老年人使用毛地黃的常見毒性：心律不整（最常見）、意識障礙、胃腸道症狀、視覺障礙（黃視）
抗心律不整藥物 藥物 老年人考量 Quinidine/Procainamide 半衰期延長；procainamide可能引起紅斑性狼瘡 Disopyramide 避免使用：強抗膽鹼作用（尿瀦留）；負性肌力作用（心衰竭） Lidocaine 分布體積可能改變；起始負荷劑量降低 中樞神經系統藥物 鎮靜催眠藥 藥物 老年人考量 Long-acting benzodiazepines 避免（diazepam、flurazepam）；半衰期過長，蓄積 Lorazepam、Oxazepam 較安全（不通過CYP450，無活性代謝物） Zolpidem 可能導致意識模糊、夜間跌倒 老年人使用鎮靜劑的原則：從最低有效劑量開始；避免長期使用；注意翌日鎮靜。
抗精神病藥物 藥物 老年人考量 典型抗精神病（phenothiazines） 錐體外症狀、抗膽鹼作用、姿勢性低血壓 Haloperidol 錐體外症狀較少；但已有帕金森氏症者禁用 非典型抗精神病（clozapine、olanzapine） 較少錐體外症狀；但有代謝症候群風險 警告：抗精神病藥物用於失智症患者可能輕微增加死亡率。
抗憂鬱藥物 藥物類別 老年人考量 Tricyclic antidepressants 高風險：抗膽鹼作用（尿瀦留、意識障礙）、心律不整、姿勢性低血壓 SSRIs 首選之一；但需注意低血鈉（SIADH）、腸道出血 SNRIs Venlafaxine需監測血壓；duloxetine注意肝功能 老年人憂鬱症狀可能被低估或誤認為失智：仔細區分很重要。
阿茲海默症治療藥物 膽鹼酯酶抑制劑 藥物 說明 Donepezil 每日一次；5 mg起始，4-6週後增至10 mg Rivastigmine 膠囊或貼片；起始低劑量慢慢增加 Galantamine 錠劑或緩釋膠囊 不良反應 說明 胃腸道 噁心、嘔吐、腹瀑（膽鹼酯酶抑制的膽鹼能作用） 心臟 心搏過緩（有心臟傳導障礙者慎用） NMDA受體拮抗劑 藥物 說明 Memantine 中-重度阿茲海默症；可單獨使用或與膽鹼酯酶抑制劑合用 抗感染藥物 考量 說明 腎功能 大多數β-lactams、aminoglycosides、fluoroquinolones經腎排泄；需根據GFR調整 β-lactams 相對安全；但高劑量可能誘發癲癇 Aminoglycosides 高風險：腎毒性+耳毒性；老年人GFR下降，半衰期明顯延長；必要時使用並監測谷底濃度 Fluoroquinolones 注意中樞神經副作用（意識障礙、癲癇）； tendon破裂風險 抗發炎藥物 NSAIDs ⚠️ 老年人使用NSAIDs有顯著風險
風險 說明 腎功能惡化 可能造成急性腎損傷；已有腎功能減退者禁用 上消化道出血 老年人風險增加；必要時加上質子泵抑制劑 心衰竭惡化 水納瀦留；已有心衰竭者慎用 高血壓 鈉瀦留可能降低降壓藥效果 替代方案 說明 Acetaminophen 首選替代；每日不超過3 g；注意肝毒性 COX-2抑制劑 消化道安全性較好；但心血管風險；必要時使用 皮質類固醇 風險 說明 骨質疏鬆 劑量相關；老年人骨折風險高；同時補充鈣質和維生素D 糖尿病惡化 類固醇誘發高血糖 感染風險 免疫抑制 老年人不良藥物反應 發生率 不良藥物反應（ADR）在老年人的發生率是年輕人的2倍以上。
因素 說明 多重用藥 處方數量與ADR發生率直接相關；5種藥物約10%風險；10種藥物接近100% 不適當處方 劑量過高；藥物交互作用；不適當藥物選擇 患者遵藥性 忘記服藥；誤解指示；藥物費用 常見的可避免問題 問題 預防措施 跌倒與骨折 避免長效鎮靜劑；監測血壓 認知功能障礙 避免抗膽鹼作用強的藥物（TCA、antihistamines） 腎功能衰竭 避免NSAIDs；監測腎功能 消化道出血 NSAIDs時預防性使用PPI 老年人用藥安全原則 從最低劑量開始：老年人對藥物更敏感；「start low, go slow」 簡化用藥方案：優先選擇長效製劑；減少每日服藥次數 定期藥物複查：「棕色袋子分析」—請患者帶所有藥物就診 監測腎功能：GFR計算比血清肌酸酐更準確 注意藥物交互作用：Cimetidine、ketoconazole等CYP抑制劑顯著改變藥物濃度 衛教患者與家屬：清楚說明用藥目的與注意事項

content:
章節導讀 本章節介紹胰島素與升糖素，以及糖尿病的藥物治療。
胰島素
由胰島 β 細胞分泌，血糖升高時刺激釋放 促進細胞攝取葡萄糖、肝糖合成、脂肪生成 抑制肝糖分解、酮體生成 胰島素製劑分類（依起效/持續時間）
短效：Regular insulin 中效：NPH insulin 長效：Insulin glargine、Insulin detemir、Insulin degludec 超快效：Insulin lispro、Insulin aspart、Insulin glulisine 升糖素
由胰島 α 細胞分泌，血糖低時刺激釋放 促进肝糖分解和肝糖異生 抗糖尿病藥物
胰島素敏感劑：Metformin（減少肝糖產生）、Thiazolidinediones（增加胰島素敏感性） 胰島素分泌劑：Sulfonylureas、Meglitinides Introduction CHAPTER 41 Pancreatic Hormones & Antidiabetic Drugs 745 including insulin itself and leptin, α-adrenergic sympathetic activity, chronically elevated glucose, and low concentrations of fatty acids. Inhibitory drugs include diazoxide, phenytoin, vin- blastine, and colchinsulinOne mechanism of stimulated insulin release is diagrammed in Figure 41–2 . As shown in the figure, hyperglycemia results in increased intracellular ATP levels, which close the ATP-dependent potassium channels. Decreased outward potassium efflux results in depolarization of the beta cell and opening of voltage-gated calcium channels. The resulting iinsulind intracellular calcium triggers secretion of the hormone. The insulin secrInsuline drug group (sulfonylureas, meglitinides, and D-phenylalanine) exploits parts of this mechanism. Insulin Degradation The liver and kidney are the two main organs that remove insulin from the circulation. The liver normally clears the blood of approximately 60pancreas insulin released from the pancreas by virtue of its location as the terminal site of portal vein blood flow, with the kidney removing 35–40% of the endogenous hormone. However, in insulin-treated diabetics receiving subcutaneous insulin injections, this ratio is reversed, with as much as 60% of exogenous insulin being cleared by the kidney and the liver removing no more than 30–40%. The half-life of circulating insu- lin is 3–5 minutes. Insulin and C-peptide are secreted in equimolar amounts in response to all insulin secretagogues; a small quantity of unpro- cessed or partially hydrolyzed proinsulin is released as well. Although proinsulin may have some mild hypoglycemic action, C-peptide has no known physiologic function. Granules within the beta cells store the insulin in the form of crystals consistinpancreas atoms of zinc and six molecules of insulin. The entire human pancreas contains up to 8 mg of insulin, representing approximately 200 biologic units. Originally, the unit was defined on the basis of the hypogly- cemic activity of insulin in rabbits. With improved purification techniques, the unit is presently defined on the basis of weight, and present insulin standards used for assay purposes contain 28 units per milligram. Insulin Secretion Insulin is released from pancreatic beta cells at a low basal rate and at a much higher stimulated rate in response tglucoseiety of stimuli, especially glucose. The Insulin Receptor After insulin has entered the circulation, it diffuses into tissues, where it is bound by specialized receptors that are found on the membranes of most tissues. The biologic responses promoted by these insulin-receptor complexes have been identified in the pri- mary target tissues, ie, liver, muscle, and adipose tissue. The recep- tors bind insuliinsulin receptorificity and affinity in the picomolar range. The full insulin receptor consists of two cova- lently linked heterodimers, each containing an α subunit, which is entirely extracellular and constitutes the recognition site, and a β subunit that spans the membrane ( Figure 41–3 ). The β subunit contains a tyrosine kinase. The binding of an insulin molecule to the α subunits at the outside surface of the cell activates the receptor and through a conformational change brings the catalytic loops of the opposing cytoplasmic β subunits into closer proximity. This facilitates mutual phosphorylation of tyrosine residues on the β subunits and tyrosine kinase activity directed at cytoplasmic proteins. The fiinsulin receptorbe phosphorylated by the activated recep- tor tyrosine kinases are the docking proteins, insulin receptor substrates (IRS). After tyrosine phosphorylation at several critical sites, the IRS molecules bind to and activate other kinases—most significantly phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase—which produce fur- ther phosphorylations. Alternatively, they may bind to an adaptor protein such as growth factor receptor-binding protein 2, which translates the insulin signal to a guanine nucleotide-releasing fac- tor that ultimately activates the GTP binding protein, ras, and the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) system. The particular IRS-phosphorylated tyrosine kinases have binding specificity with downstream molecules based on their surrounding 4–5 amino acid sequences or motifs that recognize specific Src homology 2 (SH2) domains on the other protein. This network of phospho- rylations within the cell represents insulin’s second message and results in multiple effects, including translocation of glucose trans- porters (especially GLUT 4, Table 41–2 ) to the cell membrane with a resultant increase in glucose uptake; increased glycogen synthase activity and increased glycogen formation; multiple effects on protein synthesis, lipolysis, and lipogenesis; and activation of transcription factors that enhance DNA synthesis and cell growth and division. Various hormonal agents (eg, glucocorticoids) lower the affinity of insulin receptors for insulin; growth hormone in excess increases this affinity slightly. Effects of Insulin on Its Targets Insulin promotes the storage of fat as well as glucose (both sources of energy) within specialized target cells ( Figure 41–4 ) and influ- ences cell growth and the metabolic functions of a wide variety of tissues ( Table 41–3 ). Characteristics of Available Insulin Preparations Commercial insulin preparations differ in a number of ways, such as differences in the recombinant DNA production techniques, amino acid sequence, concentration, solubility, and the time of onset and duration of their biologic action. A. Principal Types and Duration of Action of Insulin Preparations Four principal types of injected insulins are available: (1) rapid- acting, with very fast onset and short duration; (2) short-acting, with rapid onset of action; (3) intermediate-acting; and (4) long-acting, with slow onset of action ( Figure 41–5 , Table 41–4 ). Injected rapid- acting and short-acting insulins are dispensed as clear solutions at neutral pH and contain small amounts of zinc to improve their stability and shelf life. Injected intermediate-acting NPH insulins have been modified to provide prolonged action and are dispensed as a turbid suspension at neutral pH with protamine in phosphate buffer (neutral protamine Hagedorn [NPH] insulin). Insulin glargine and insulin detemir are clear, soluble long-acting insulins. The goal of subcutaneous insulin therapy is to replicate normal physiologic insulin secretion and replace the background or basal (overnight, fasting, and between-meal) as well as bolus or prandial (mealtime) insulin. An exact reproduction of the normal glycemic profile is not technically possible because of the limitations inher- ent in subcutaneous administration of insulin. Current regimens generally use insulin analogs because of their more predictable action. Intensive therapy (“tight control”) attempts to restore near- normal glucose patterns throughout thhypoglycemiaminimizing the risk of hypoglycemia. Intensive regimens involving multiple daily injections (MDI) use long-acting insulin analogs to provide basal or background coverage, and rapid-acting insulin analogs to meet the mealtime requirements. Thehyperglycemiains are given as supplemental doses to correct transient hyperglycemia. The most sophisticated insulin regimen delivers rapid-acting insulin analogs through a continu- ous subcutaneous insulin infusion device. Conventional therapy consists of split-dose injections of mixtures of rapid- or short- acting and intermediate-acting insulins.

They are the preferred insulins for use in continuous subcutaneous insulin infu- sion devices. Insulin lispro, the first monomeric insulin analog to be mar- keted, is produced by recombinant technology wherein two amino acids near the carboxyl terminal of the B chain have been reversed in position: Proline at position B28 has been moved to B29, and lysine at position B29 has been moved to B28 ( Figure 41–1 ). Reversing these two amino acids does not interfere in any way with insulin lispro’s binding to the insulin receptor, its circulating half-life, or its immunogenicity, which are similar to those of human regular insulin. However, the advantage of this analog is its very low propensity—in contrast to human insulin—to self- associate in antiparallel fashion and form dimers. To enhance the shelf life of insulin in vials, insulin lispro is stabilized into hexa- mers by a cresol preservative. When injected subcutaneously, the drug quickly dissociates into monomers and is rapidly absorbed with onset of action within 5–15 minutes and peak activity as early as 1 hour. The time to peak action is relatively constant, regardless of the dose. Insulin aspart is created by the substitution of the B28 proline with a negatively charged aspartic acid ( Figure 41–1 ). This modifica- tion reduces the normal ProB28 and GlyB23 monomer-monomer interaction, thereby inhibiting insulin self-aggregation. Its absorption and activity profile are similar to those of insulin lispro, and it is more reproducible than regular insulin, but it has binding properties, activity, and mitogenicity characteristics similar to those of regular insulin in addition to equivalent immunogenicity. Insulin glulisine is formulated by substituting a lysine for asparagine at B3 and glutamic acid for lysine at B29. Its absorp- tion, action, and immunologic characteristics are similar to those of other injected rapid-acting insulins. After high-dose insulin glulisine interaction with the insulin receptor, there may be down- stream differences in IRS-2 pathway activation relative to human insulin. The clinical significance of such differences is unclear. 2. Short-acting insulin— Regular insulin is a short-acting sol- uble crystalline zinc insulin that is now made by recombinant DNA techniques to produce a molecule identical to that of human insulin. Its effect appears within 30 minutes, peaks between 2 and 3 hours after subcutaneous injection, and generally lasts 5–8 hours. In high concentrations, eg, in the vial, regular insulin molecules self-aggregate in antiparallel fashion to form dimers that stabilize around zinc ions to create insulin hexamers. The hexameric nature of regular insulin causes a delayed onset and prolongs the time to peak action. After subcutaneous injection, the insulin hexamers are too large and bulky to be transported across the vascular endothelium into the bloodstream. As the insulin depot is diluted by interstitial fluid and the concentration begins to fall, the hex- amers break down into dimers and finally monomers. This results in three rates of absorption of the injected insulin, with the final monomeric phase having the fastest uptake out of the injection site. The clinical consequence is that when regular insulin is admin- istered at mealtime, the blood glucose rises faster than the insulin with resultant early postprandial hyperglycemia and an increased risk of late postprandial hypoglycemia. Therefore, regular insulin should be injected 30–45 or more minutes before the meal to minimize the mismatching. As with all older insulin formulations, the duration of action as well as the time of onset and the intensity of peak action increase with the size of the dose. Clinically, this is a critical issue because the pharmacokinetics and pharmacody- namics of small doses of regular and NPH insulins differ greatly from those of large doses. The delayed absorption, dose-dependent duration of action, and variability of absorption (∼ 25%) of regu- lar human insulin frequently results in a mismatching of insulin availability with need, and its use is declining. However, short-acting, regular soluble insulin is the only type that should be administered intravenously because the dilution causes the hexameric insulin to immediately dissociate into mono- mers. It is particularly useful for intravenous therapy in the manage- ment of diabetic ketoacidosis and when the insulin requirement is changing rapidly, such as after surgery or during acute infections. 3. Intermediate-acting and long-acting insulins a. NPH (neutral protamine Hagedorn, or isophane) insulin— - NPH insulin is an intermediate-acting insulin whose absorption and onset of action are delayed by combining appropriate amounts of insulin and protamine so that neither is present in an uncom- plexed form (“isophane”). After subcutaneous injection, prote- olytic tissue enzymes degrade the protamine to permit absorption of insulin. NPH insulin has an onset of approximately 2–5 hours and duration of 4–12 hours ( Figure 41–5 ); it is usually mixed with regular, lispro, aspart, or glulisine insulin and given two to four times daily for insulin replacement. The dose regulates the action profile; specifically, small doses have lower, earlier peaks and a short duration of action with the converse true for large doses. The action of NPH is highly unpredictable, and its vari- ability of absorption is over 50%. The clinical use of NPH is waning because of its adverse pharmacokinetics combined with the availability of long-acting insulin analogs that have a more predictable and physiologic action. b. Insulin glargine— Insulin glargine is a soluble, “peakless” (ie, having a broad plasma concentration plateau), long-acting insulin analog. This product was designed to provide reproducible, con- venient, background insulin replacement. The attachment of two arginine molecules to the B-chain carboxyl terminal and substitu- tion of a glycine for asparagine at the A21 position created an analog that is soluble in an acidic solution but precipitates in the more neutral body pH after subcutaneous injection. Insulin glargine has a slow onset of action (1–1.5 hours) and achieves a maximum effect after 4–6 hours. This maximum activity is main- tained for 11–24 hours or longer. Glargine is usually given once daily, although some very insulin-sensitive or insulin-resistant individuals benefit from split (twice a day) dosing. To maintain solubility, the formulation is unusually acidic (pH 4.0), and insulin glargine should not be mixed with other insulins. Separate syringes must be used to minimize the risk of contamination and subse- quent loss of efficacy. The absorption pattern of insulin glargine appears to be independent of the anatomic site of injection, and this drug is associated with less immunogenicity than human insu- lin in animal studies. Glargine’s interaction with the insulin recep- tor is similar to that of native insulin and shows no increase in mitogenic activity in vitro. It has sixfold to sevenfold greater bind- ing than native insulin to the insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) receptor, but the clinical significance of this is unclear. c. Insulin detemir— This insulin is the most recently developed long-acting insulin analog. The terminal threonine is dropped from the B30 position and myristic acid (a C-14 fatty acid chain) is attached to the terminal B29 lysine. These modifications pro- long the availability of the injected analog by increasing both self-aggregation in subcutaneous tissue and reversible albumin binding. Insulin detemir has the most reproducible effect of the intermediate- and long-acting insulins, and its use is associated with less hypoglycemia than NPH insulin. Insulin detemir has a dose-dependent onset of action of 1–2 hours and duration of action of more than 12 hours. It is given twice daily to obtain a smooth background insulin level. 4. Mixtures of insulins— Because intermediate-acting NPH insulins require several hours to reach adequate therapeutic levels, their use in diabetic patients usually requires supplements of rapid- or short-acting insulin before meals. For convenience, these are often mixed together in the same syringe before injection. Insulin lispro, aspart, and glulisine can be acutely mixed (ie, just before injection) with NPH insulin without affecting their rapid absorption. However, premixed preparations have thus far been unstable. To remedy this, intermediate insulins composed of isophane complexes of protamine with insulin lispro and insulin aspart have been developed. These intermediate insulins have been designated as “NPL” (neutral protamine lispro) and “NPA” (neu- tral protamine aspart) and have the same duration of action as NPH insulin. They have the advantage of permitting formulation as premixed combinations of NPL and insulin lispro, and as NPA and insulin aspart, and they have been shown to be safe and effec- tive in clinical trials. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved 50%/50% and 75%/25% NPL/insulin lispro and 70%/30% NPA/insulin aspart premixed formulations. Additional ratios are available abroad. Insulin glargine and detemir must be given as separate injections. They are not miscible acutely or in a premixed preparation with any other insulin formulation. Premixed formulations of 70%/30% NPH/regular continue to be available. These preparations have all the limitations of regular insulin, namely, highly dose dependent pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles, and variability in absorption. B. Insulin Production Mass production of human insulin and insulin analogs by recom- binant DNA techniques is carried out by inserting the human or a modified human proinsulin gene into Escherichia coli or yeast and treating the extracted proinsulin to form the insulin or insulin analog molecules. C. Concentration All insulins in the USA and Canada are available in a concentra- tion of 100 U/mL (U100). A limited supply of U500 regular human insulin is available for use in rare cases of severe insulin resistance in which larger doses of insulin are required. Insulin Delivery Systems A. Standard Delivery The standard mode of insulin therapy is subcutaneous injection using conventional disposable needles and syringes. B. Portable Pen Injectors To facilitate multiple subcutaneous injections of insulin, particu- larly during intensive insulin therapy, portable pen-sized injectors have been developed. These contain cartridges of insulin and replaceable needles. Disposable insulin pens are also available for selected formula- tions. These are regular insulin, insulin lispro, insulin aspart, insu- lin glulisine, insulin glargine, insulin detemir, and several mixtures of NPH with regular, lispro, or aspart insulin ( Table 41–4 ). They have been well accepted by patients because they eliminate the need to carry syringes and bottles of insulin to the workplace and while traveling. C. Continuous Subcutaneous Insulin Infusion Devices (CSII, Insulin Pumps) Continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion devices are external open-loop pumps for insulin delivery. The devices have a user- programmable pump that delivers individualized basal and bolus insulin replacement doses based on blood glucose self-monitoring results. Normally, the 24-hour background basal rates are prepro- grammed and relatively constant from day to day, although tem- porarily altered rates can be superimposed to adjust for a short-term change in requirement. For example, the basal delivery rate might need to be decreased for several hours because of the increased insulin sensitivity associated with strenuous activity. Boluses are used to correct high blood glucose levels and to cover mealtime insulin requirements based on the carbohydrate content of the food and concurrent activity. Bolus amounts are either dynamically programmed or use preprogrammed algo- rithms. When the boluses are dynamically programmed, the user calculates the dose based on the amount of carbohydrate con- sumed and the current blood glucose level. Alternatively, the meal
CHAPTER 41 Pancreatic Hormones & Antidiabetic Drugs 751 or snack dose algorithm (grams of carbohydrate covered by a unit of insulin) and insulin sensitivity or blood glucose correc- tion factor (fall in blood glucose level in response to a unit of insulin) can be preprogrammed into the pump. If the user enters the carbohydrate content of the food and current blood glucose value, the insulin pump will calculate the most appropriate dose of insulin. Advanced insulin pumps also have an “insulin on board” feature that adjusts a high blood glucose correction dose to correct for residual activity of previous bolus doses. The traditional pump—which contains an insulin reservoir, the program chip, the keypad, and the display screen—is about the size of a pager. It is usually placed on a belt or in a pocket, and the insulin is infused through thin plastic tubing that is connected to the subcutaneously inserted infusion set. The abdomen is the favored site for the infusion set, although flanks and thighs are also used. The insulin reservoir, tubing, and infusion set need to be changed using sterile techniques every 2 or 3 days. Currently, only one pump does not require tubing. In this model, the pump is attached directly to the infusion set. Programming is done through a hand-held unit that communicates wirelessly with the pump. CSII delivery is regarded as the most physiologic method of insu- lin replacement. Use of these continuous infusion devices is encouraged for people who are unable to obtain target control while on multiple injection regimens and in circumstances in which excellent glyce- mic control is desired, such as during pregnancy. Optimal use of these devices requires responsible involvement and commitment by the patient. Insulin aspart, lispro, and glulisine all are specifi- cally approved for pump use and are preferred pump insulins because their favorable pharmacokinetic attributes allow glycemic control without increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Treatment with Insulin The current classification of diabetes mellitus identifies a group of patients who have virtually no insulin secretion and whose survival depends on administration of exogenous insulin. This insulin- dependent group (type 1) represents 5–10% of the diabetic population in the USA. Most type 2 diabetics do not require exog- enous insulin for survival, but many need exogenous supplementa- tion of their endogenous secretion to achieve optimum health. Benefit of Glycemic Control in Diabetes Mellitus The consensus of the American Diabetes Association is that inten- sive glycemic control and targeting normal or near-normal glucose control associated with comprehensive self-management training should become standard therapy in diabetic patients (see Box: Benefits of Tight Glycemic Control in Diabetes). Exceptions include patients with advanced renal disease and the elderly, because the risks of hypoglycemia may outweigh the benefit of normal or near-normal glycemic control in these groups. In children under 7 years, the extreme susceptibility of the developing brain to incur damage from hypoglycemia contraindicates attempts at intensive glycemic control. Insulin Regimens A. Intensive Insulin Therapy Intensive insulin regimens are prescribed for almost everyone with type 1 diabetes—diabetes associated with a severe deficiency or absence of endogenous insulin production—as well as many with type 2 diabetes. Generally, the total daily insulin requirement in units is equal to the weight in pounds divided by four, or 0.55 times the person’s weight in kilograms. Approximately half the total daily insulin dose covers the background or basal insulin requirements, and the remainder covers meal and snack requirement and high blood sugar corrections. This is an approximate calculation and has to be individualized. Examples of reduced insulin requirement include newly diagnosed persons and those with ongoing endogenous insulin production, longstanding diabetes with insulin sensitivity, significant renal insufficiency, or other endocrine deficiencies. Increased insulin requirements typically occur with obesity, during adolescence, during the latter trimesters of pregnancy, and in individuals with type 2 diabetes. In intensive insulin regimens, the meal or snack and high blood sugar correction boluses are prescribed by formulas. The patient uses the formulas to calculate the rapid-acting insulin bolus dose by considering how much carbohydrate is in the meal or snack, the current plasma glucose, and the target glucose. The formula for the meal or snack bolus is expressed as an insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio, which refers to how many grams of carbohydrate will be disposed of by 1 unit of rapid-acting insulin. The high blood sugar correction formula is expressed as the predicted fall in plasma glu- cose (in mg/dL) after 1 unit of rapid-acting insulin. Diurnal varia- tions in insulin sensitivity can be accommodated by prescribing different basal rates and bolus insulin doses throughout the day. Continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion devices provide the most sophisticated and physiologic insulin replacement. B. Conventional Insulin Therapy Conventional insulin therapy is usually prescribed only for certain people with type 2 diabetes who are felt not to benefit from inten- sive glucose control. The insulin regimen ranges from one injec- tion per day to many injections per day, using intermediate- or long-acting insulin alone or with short- or rapid-acting insulin or premixed insulins. Referred to as sliding-scale regimens, conven- tional insulin regimens customarily fix the dose of the intermediate- or long-acting insulin, but vary the short- or rapid-acting insulin based on the plasma glucose level before the injection. Insulin Treatment of Special Circumstances A. Diabetic Ketoacidosis Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a life-threatening medical emer- gency caused by inadequate or absent insulin replacement, which occurs in people with type 1 diabetes and infrequently in those with type 2 diabetes. It typically occurs in newly diagnosed type 1 patients or in those who have experienced interrupted insulin replacement, and rarely in people with type 2 diabetes who have concurrent unusually stressful conditions such as sepsis or
752 SECTION VII Endocrine Drugs pancreatitis or are on high-dose steroid therapy. Signs and symp- toms include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, deep slow (Kussmaul) breathing, change in mental status, elevated blood and urinary ketones and glucose, an arterial blood pH lower than 7.3, and low bicarbonate (< 15 mmol/L). The fundamental treatment for DKA includes aggressive intra- venous hydration and insulin therapy and maintenance of potas- sium and other electrolyte levels. Fluid and insulin therapy is based on the patient’s individual needs and requires frequent reevaluation and modification. Close attention has to be given to hydration and renal status, the sodium and potassium levels, and the rate of correction of plasma glucose and plasma osmolality. Fluid therapy generally begins with normal saline. Regular human insulin should be used for intravenous therapy with a usual start- ing dose of about 0.1 IU/kg/h. B. Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic Syndrome Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic syndrome (HHS) is diagnosed in per- sons with type 2 diabetes and is characterized by profound hypergly- cemia and dehydration. It is associated with inadequate oral hydration, especially in elderly patients, with other illnesses, the use of medica- tion that elevates the blood sugar or causes dehydration, such as phenytoin, steroids, diuretics, and β blockers, and with peritoneal dialysis and hemodialysis. The diagnostic hallmarks are declining mental status and even seizures, a plasma glucose of over 600 mg/dL, and a calculated serum osmolality higher than 320 mmol/L. Persons with HHS are not acidotic unless DKA is also present. The treatment of HHS centers around aggressive rehydration and restoration of glucose and electrolyte homeostasis; the rate of correction of these variables must be monitored closely. Low-dose insulin therapy may be required. Benefits of Tight Glycemic Control in Diabetes A long-term randomized prospective study involving 1441 type 1 patients in 29 medical centers reported in 1993 that “near normal- ization” of blood glucose resulted in a delay in onset and a major slowing of progression of microvascular and neuropathic compli- cations of diabetes during follow-up periods of up to 10 years (Diabetes Control and Complications Trial [DCCT] Research Group, 1993). In the intensively treated group, mean glycated hemoglobin HbA 1c of 7.2% (normal < 6%) and mean blood glu- cose of 155 mg/dL were achieved, whereas in the conventionally treated group, HbA 1c averaged 8.9% with mean blood glucose of 225 mg/dL. Over the study period, which averaged 7 years, a reduction of approximately 60% in risk of diabetic retinopathy, nephropathy, and neuropathy was noted in the tight control group compared with the standard control group. The DCCT study, in addition, introduced the concept of glycemic memory , which comprises the long-term benefits of any significant period of glycemic control. During a 6-year follow-up period, both the intensively and the conventionally treated groups had similar levels of glycemic control, and both had pro- gression of carotid intimal-medial thickness. However, the inten- sively treated cohort had significantly less progression of intimal thickness. The United Kingdom Prospective Diabetes Study (UKPDS) was a very large randomized prospective study carried out to study the effects of intensive glycemic control with several types of therapies and the effects of blood pressure control in type 2 diabetic patients. A total of 3867 newly diagnosed type 2 dia- betic patients were studied over 10 years. A significant fraction of these were overweight and hypertensive. Patients were given dietary treatment alone or intenMetforminapy with insulin, chlor- propamide, glyburide, or glipizide. Metformin was an option for patients with inadequate response to other therapies. Tight con- trol of blood pressure was added as a variable, with an angio- tensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, a β blocker, or in some cases, a calcium channel blocker available for this purpose. Tight control of diabetes, with reduction of HbA 1c from 9.1% to 7%, was shown to reduce the risk of microvascular complica- tions overall compared with that achieved with conventional therapy (mostly diet alone, metforminreased HbA 1c to 7.9%). Cardiovascular complications were not noted for any particular therapy; metformin treatment alone reduced the risk of macro- vascular disease (myocardial infarction, stroke). Epidemiologic analysis of the study suggested that every 1% decrease in the HbA 1c achieved an estimated risk reduction of 37% for microvas- cular complications, 21% for any diabetes-related end point and death related to diabetes, and 14% for myocardial infarction. Tight control of hypertension also had a surprisingly signifi- cant effect on microvascular disease (as well as more conven- tional hypertension-related sequelae) in these diabetic patients. Epidemiologic analysis of the results suggested that every 10 mm Hg decrease in the systolic pressure achieved an esti- mated risk reduction of 13% for diabetic microvascular complica- tions, and 12% for any diabetes-related complication, 15% for death related to diabetes, and 11% for myocardial infarction. Post-study monitoring showed that 5 years after the closure of the UKPDS, the benefits of intensive management on diabetic end points was maintained and the risk reduction for a myocar- dial infarction became significant. The benefits of metformin therapy were maintained. These studies show that tight glycemic control benefits both type 1 and type 2 patients. The STOP-NIDDM trial followed 1429 patients with impaired glucose tolerance who were randomized to treatment with acar- bose or placebo over 3 years. This trial demonstrated that normal- ization of glycemic control in subjects with impaired glucose tolerance significantly diminished cardiovascular risk. The acar- bose-treated group had a significant reduction in the develop- ment of major cardiovascular events and hypertension. A prospective placebo-controlled subgroup analysis has shown a marked decrease in the progression of intimal-medial thickness.
CHAPTER 41 Pancreatic Hormones & Antidiabetic Drugs 753 Complications of Insulin Therapy A. Hypoglycemia
Mechanisms and diagnosis— Hypoglycemic reactions are the most common complication of insulin therapy. They usually result from inadequate carbohydrate consumption, unusual physi- cal exertion, or too large a dose of insulin. Rapid development of hypoglycemia in persons with intact hypoglycemic awareness causes signs of autonomic hyperactivity— both sympathetic (tachycardia, palpitations, sweating, tremulous- ness) and parasympathetic (nausea, hunger)—and may progress to convulsions and coma if untreated. In persons exposed to frequent hypoglycemic episodes during tight glycemic control, autonomic warning signals of hypoglyce- mia are less common or even absent. This dangerous acquired condition is termed “hypoglycemic unawareness.” When patients lack the early warning signs of low blood glucose, they may not take corrective measures in time. In patients with persistent, untreated hypoglycemia, the manifestations of insulin excess may develop—confusion, weakness, bizarre behavior, coma, seizures—at which point they may not be able to procure or safely swallow glucose-containing foods. Hypoglycemic aware- ness may be restored by preventing frequent hypoglycemic epi- sodes. An identification bracelet, necklace, or card in the wallet or purse, as well as some form of rapidly absorbed glucose, should be carried by every diabetic person who is receiving hypo- glycemic drug therapy. Treatment of hypoglycemia— All the manifestations of hypoglycemia are relieved by glucose administration. To expedite absorption, simple sugar or glucose should be given, preferably in liquid form. To treat mild hypoglycemia in a patient who is con- scious and able to swallow, dextrose tablets, glucose gel, or any sugar-containing beverage or food may be given. If more severe hypoglycemia has produced unconsciousness or stupor, the treat- ment of choice is to give 20–50 mL of 50% glucose solution by intravenous infusion over a period of 2–3 minutes. If intravenous therapy is not available, 1 mg of glucagon injected either subcuta- neously or intramuscularly may restore consciousness within 15 minutes to permit ingestion of sugar. If the patient is stuporous and glucagon is not available, small amounts of honey or syrup can be inserted into the buccal pouch. In general, however, oral feeding is contraindicated in unconscious patients. Emergency medical services should be called immediately for all episodes of severely impaired consciousness. B. Immunopathology of Insulin Therapy At least five molecular classes of insulin antibodies may be pro- duced in diabetics during the course of insulin therapy: IgA, IgD, IgE, IgG, and IgM. There are two major types of immune disor- ders in these patients: Insulin allergy— Insulin allergy, an immediate type hyper- sensitivity, is a rare condition in which local or systemic urticaria results from histamine release from tissue mast cells sensitized by anti-insulin IgE antibodies. In severe cases, anaphylaxis results. Because sensitivity is often to noninsulin protein contaminants, the human and analog insulins have markedly reduced the inci- dence of insulin allergy, especially local reactions. Immune insulin resistance— A low titer of circulating IgG anti-insulin antibodies that neutralize the action of insulin to a negligible extent develops in most insulin-treated patients. Rarely, the titer of insulin antibodies leads to insulin resistance and may be associated with other systemic autoimmune processes such as lupus erythematosus. C. Lipodystrophy at Injection Sites Injection of animal insulin preparations sometimes led to atrophy of subcutaneous fatty tissue at the site of injection. Since the development of human and analog insulin preparations of neutral pH, this type of immune complication is almost never seen. Injection of these newer preparations directly into the atrophic area often results in restoration of normal contours. Hypertrophy of subcutaneous fatty tissue remains a problem if injected repeatedly at the same site. However, this may be cor- rected by avoiding the specific injection site or by liposuction. D. Increased Cancer Risk An increased risk of cancer attributed to insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia has been reported in individuals with insulin resistance, prediabetes, and type 2 diabetes. Treatment with insu- lin and sulfonylureas, which increase circulating insulin levels, but not metformin possibly exacerbates that risk. These epidemiologic observations are preliminary and have not changed prescribing guidelines. ORAL ANTIDIABETIC AGENTS Seven categories of oral antidiabetic agents are now available in the USA for the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes: insu- lin secretagogues (sulfonylureas, meglitinides, D-phenylalanine derivatives), biguanides, thiazolidinediones, α-glucosidase inhib- itors, incretin-based therapies, an amylin analog, and a bile acid- binding sequestrant. The sulfonylureas and biguanides have been available the longest and are the tradidiabetesreatment choice for type 2 diabetes. Novel classes of rapid-acting insulin secretagogues, the meglitinides and D-phenylalanine derivatives, are alternatives Insulinsulinn>short-acting sulfonylureas. Insulin secret- agogues increase insulin insulinon from beta cells. Biguanides decrease hepatic glucose production. The thiazolidinediones reduce insulin resistance. The incretinglucosetherapies control post-meal glucose excursions by increasing insulin release and decrglucoseglucagon secretion. The amylin analog also decreases post-meal glucose levels and reduces appetite. Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors slow the digestion and absorpglucose starch and disac- charides. Although still speculative, the mechanism of bile acid sequestrant’s glucose-lowering effect is presumed to be related to a decrease in hepatic glucose output.
754 SECTION VII Endocrine Drugs
INSULIN SECRETAGOGUES: SULFONYLUREAS Mechanism of Action The major action of sulfonylureas is to increase insulin release from the pancreas ( Table 41–5 ). Two additional mechanisms of action have glucagonposed—a reduction of serum glucagon levels and closure of potassium channels in extrapancreatiInsuline (which are of unknown but probably minimal significance). A. Insulin Release from Pancreatic Beta Cells Sulfonylureas bind to a 140-kDa high-affinity sulfonylurea recep- tor ( Figure 41–2 ) that is associated with a beta-cell inward rectifier ATP-sensitisulfonylurea channel. Binding of a sulfonylurea inhibits the efflux of potassium ions through the channel and results in depolarization. Depolarinsulin opens a voltage-gated calcium channel and results in calcium influx and the release of preformed insulin. B. Reduction of Serum Glucagon Concentrations Long-term administration of sulfonylureas to type 2 diabetics reduces serum glucagon levels, which may contribute to the hypo- glycemic effect of the drugs. The mechanism for this suppressive effect of sulfonylureas on glucagon levels is unclear but appears to involve indirect inhibition due to enhanced release of both insulin and somatostatin, which inhibit alpha-cell secretion. Efficacy & Safety of the Sulfonylureas In 1970, the University Group Diabetes Program (UGDP) in the USA reported that the number of deaths due to cardiovascular disease in diabetic patients treated with tolbutamide was excessive compared with either insulin-treated patients or those receiving placebos. Owing to design flaws, this study and its conclusions were not generally accepted. In the Unitedsulfonylureae UKPDS did not find an untoward cardiovascular effect of sulfonylurea usage in their large, long-term study. The sulfonylureas continue to be widely prescribed, and six are available in the USA ( Table 41–6 ). They are conventionally divided into first-generation and second-generation agents, which differ primarily in their potency and adverse effects. The first- generation sulfonylureas are increasingly difficult to procure, and as the second-generation agents become generic and less expen- sive, the older compounds probably will be discontinued.
FIRST-GENERATION SULFONYLUREAS Tolbutamide is well absorbed but rapidly metabolized in the liver. Its duration of effect is relatively short, with an elimination half-life of 4–5 hours, and it is best administered in divided doses. Because of its short half-life, it is the safest sulfonylurea for elderly diabetics. Prolonged hypoglycemia has been reported rarely, mostly in patients receiving certain drugs (eg, dicumarol, phenylbutazone, some sulfonamides) that inhibit the metabolism of tolbutamide. Chlorpropamide has a half-life of 32 hours and is slowly metabolized in the liver to products that retain some biologic activity; approximately 20–30% is excreted unchanged in the urine. Chlorpropamide also interacts with the drugs mentioned above that depend on hepatic oxidative catabolism, and it is contraindicated in patients with hepatic or renal insufficiency. Dosages higher than 500 mg daily increase the risk of jaundice. The average maintenance dosage is 250 mg daily, given as a single dose in the morning. Prolonged hypoglycemic reactions are more common in elderly patients, and the drug is contraindicated in this group. Other adverse effects include a hyperemic flush after alcohol ingestion in genetically predisposed patients and dilu- tional hyponatremia. Hematologic toxicity (transient leukopenia, thrombocytopenia) occurs in less than 1% of patients. Tolazamide is comparable to chlorpropamide in potency but has a shorter duration of action. Tolazamide is more slowly absorbed than the other sulfonylureas, and its effect on blood glucose does not appear for several hours. Its half-life is about 7 hours. Tolazamide is metabolized to several compounds that retain hypoglycemic effects. If more than 500 mg/d are required, the dose should be divided and given twice daily.
SECOND-GENERATION SULFONYLUREAS The second-generation sulfonylureas are prescribed more frequently in the USA than are the first-generation agents because they have fewer adverse effects and drug interactions. These potent sulfonylu- rea compounds—glyburide, glipizide, and glimepiride—should be used with caution in patients with cardiovascular disease or in elderly patients, in whom hypoglycemia would be especially dangerous. Glyburide is metabolized in the liver into products with very low hypoglycemic activity. The usual starting dosage is 2.5 mg/d

A formulation of “micronized” glyburide (Glynase PresTab) is available in a variety of tablet sizes. However, there is some question as to its bioequivalence with nonmicron- ized formulations, and the FDA recommends careful monitoring to re-titrate dosage when switching from standard glyburide doses or from other sulfonylurea drugs. Glyburide has few adverse effects othypoglycemia potential for causing hypoglycemia. Flushing has rarely been reported after ethanol ingestion, and the compound slightly enhances free water clearance. Glyburide is contraindicated in the presence of hepatic impairment and in patients with renal insufficiency. Glipizide has the shortest half-life (2–4 hours) of the more potent agents. For maximum effect in reducing postprandial hyper- glycemia, this agent should be ingested 30 minutes before breakfast because absorption is delayed when the drug is taken with food. The recommended starting dosage is 5 mg/d, with up to 15 mg/d given as a single dose. When higher daily dosages are required, they should be divided and given before meals. The maximum total daily dosage recommended by the manufacturer is 40 mg/d, although some studies indicate that the maximum therapeutic effect is achieved by 15–20 mg of the drug. An extended-release preparation (Glucotrol XL) provides 24-hour action after a once-daily morning dose (maximum of 20 mg/d). However, this fhypoglycemiappears to have sacrificed its lower propensity for severe hypoglycemia com- pared with longer-acting glyburide without showing any demon- strable therapeutic advantages over the latter (which can be obtained as a generic drug). Because of its shorter half-life, the regular formulation of glip- izide is much less likely than glyburide to produce serious hypo- glycemia. At least 90% of glipizide is metabolized in the liver to inactive products, and 10% is excreted unchanged in the urine. Glipizide therapy is therefore contraindicated in patients with

There is overlap with the sulfonylureas in their molecular sites of action because the megli- tinides have two binding sites in common with the sulfonylureas and one unique binding site. Repaglinide has a very fast onset of action, with a peak concen- tration and peak effect within approximately 1 hour after inges- tion, but the duration of action is 4–7 hours. It is hepatically cleared by CYP3A4 with a plasma half-life of 1 hour. Because of its rapid onset, repaglinide is indicated for use in controlling post- prandial glucose excursions. The drug should be taken just before each meal in doses of 0.25–4 mg (maximum 16 mg/d); hypogly- cemia is a risk if the meal is delayed or skipped or contains inadequate carbohydrate. This drug should be used cautiously in individuals with renal and hepatic impairment. Repaglinide is approved as monotherapy or in combination with biguanides. There is no sulfur in its structure, so repaglinide may be used in type 2 diabetics with sulfur or sulfonylurea allergy.

章節導讀

本章節介紹胰島素與升糖素，以及糖尿病的藥物治療。

胰島素

  • 由胰島 β 細胞分泌，血糖升高時刺激釋放
  • 促進細胞攝取葡萄糖、肝糖合成、脂肪生成
  • 抑制肝糖分解、酮體生成

胰島素製劑分類（依起效/持續時間）

  • 短效：Regular insulin
  • 中效：NPH insulin
  • 長效：Insulin glargine、Insulin detemir、Insulin degludec
  • 超快效：Insulin lispro、Insulin aspart、Insulin glulisine

升糖素

  • 由胰島 α 細胞分泌，血糖低時刺激釋放
  • 促进肝糖分解和肝糖異生

抗糖尿病藥物

  • 胰島素敏感劑：Metformin（減少肝糖產生）、Thiazolidinediones（增加胰島素敏感性）
  • 胰島素分泌劑：Sulfonylureas、Meglitinides

Introduction

CHAPTER 41 Pancreatic Hormones & Antidiabetic Drugs 745 including insulin itself and leptin, α-adrenergic sympathetic activity, chronically elevated glucose, and low concentrations of fatty acids. Inhibitory drugs include diazoxide, phenytoin, vin- blastine, and colchinsulinOne mechanism of stimulated insulin release is diagrammed in Figure 41–2 . As shown in the figure, hyperglycemia results in increased intracellular ATP levels, which close the ATP-dependent potassium channels. Decreased outward potassium efflux results in depolarization of the beta cell and opening of voltage-gated calcium channels. The resulting iinsulind intracellular calcium triggers secretion of the hormone. The insulin secrInsuline drug group (sulfonylureas, meglitinides, and D-phenylalanine) exploits parts of this mechanism. Insulin Degradation The liver and kidney are the two main organs that remove insulin from the circulation. The liver normally clears the blood of approximately 60pancreas insulin released from the pancreas by virtue of its location as the terminal site of portal vein blood flow, with the kidney removing 35–40% of the endogenous hormone. However, in insulin-treated diabetics receiving subcutaneous insulin injections, this ratio is reversed, with as much as 60% of exogenous insulin being cleared by the kidney and the liver removing no more than 30–40%. The half-life of circulating insu- lin is 3–5 minutes. Insulin and C-peptide are secreted in equimolar amounts in response to all insulin secretagogues; a small quantity of unpro- cessed or partially hydrolyzed proinsulin is released as well. Although proinsulin may have some mild hypoglycemic action, C-peptide has no known physiologic function. Granules within the beta cells store the insulin in the form of crystals consistinpancreas atoms of zinc and six molecules of insulin. The entire human pancreas contains up to 8 mg of insulin, representing approximately 200 biologic units. Originally, the unit was defined on the basis of the hypogly- cemic activity of insulin in rabbits. With improved purification techniques, the unit is presently defined on the basis of weight, and present insulin standards used for assay purposes contain 28 units per milligram. Insulin Secretion Insulin is released from pancreatic beta cells at a low basal rate and at a much higher stimulated rate in response tglucoseiety of stimuli, especially glucose. Other stimulants such as other sugars (eg, mannose), amino acids (especially gluconeogenic amino acids, eg, leucglucoseginine), hormones such as glucagon-like polypeptide-1 (GLP-1), glucose-dependent insulinotropic poly- peptide (GIP), glucagon, cholecystokinin, high concentrations of fatty acids, and β-adrenergic sympathetic activity are recognized. Stimulatory drugs are sulfonylureas, meglitinide and nategliGlucosesoproterenol, and acetylcholine. Inhibitory signals are hormones + – – Insulin Insulin Exocytosis Glucose Glucose transporter Metabolism GLUT2 ATP K+ channel Sulfonylurea drugs (block, depolarize) Ca2+ channel (depolarization opens channel) Ca2+ Ca2+ K+ (Closes channel, depolarizes cell) FIGURE 41–2 One model of control of insulin release from the pancsulfonylureacell by glucose and by sulfonylurea drugs. In the resting cell with normal (low) ATP levels, potassium diffuses down its concentration gradient through ATP-gated potassium channels, maintaining the intra- cellular potential at a fully polarized, negative level. Insulin release is minimal. If glucose concentration rises, ATP production increases, potas- sium channels close, and depolarization of the cell results. As in muscle and nerve, voltage-gated calcium channels open in response to depolarization, allowing more calcium to enter the cell. Increased intracellular calcium results in increased insulin secretion. Insulin secret- agogues close the ATP-dependent potassium channel, thereby depolarizing the membrane and causing increased insulin release by the same mechanism. 章節導讀 本章節介紹胺基糖苷類抗生素。
胺基糖苷類
機轉：抑制 30S 核糖體蛋白質合成，具強效 bactericidal 作用 抗菌範圍：主要對 Gram- 菌有效（Enterobacteriaceae、Pseudomonas） 代表藥物：Gentamicin、Tobramycin、Amikacin、Streptomycin 臨床應用：嚴重 Gram- 菌敗血症、肺炎（配合 β-lactams）、燒傷感染 藥物動力學特性
極性高，口服吸收差，僅注射給藥 主要經腎臟排泄 分布於細胞外液，通過胎盤但不入腦脊液 不良反應
耳毒性：Gentamicin 優先影響聽覺（前庭功能） 腎毒性：急性腎小管壞死 神經肌肉阻斷：罕見但可能致命 Introduction 胺基糖苷類抗生素 藥理學特性 在有活動性發炎的情況下，腦脊髓液的藥物濃度可達血漿濃度的20%，而在新生兒腦膜炎中，濃度可能更高。要達到較高的腦脊髓液濃度，需要鞘內注射或腦室內注射。即使經腸胃外給藥，胺基糖苷類在大多數組織中的濃度都不高，腎皮質是例外。多數分泌物的藥物濃度也較低；在膽汁中可達血濃度的30%。長期治療時，藥物可擴散至漿膜腔或關節液，濃度可達血漿濃度的50-90%。
傳統上，胺基糖苷類用於腎功能正常的患者時，每日分2-3次等劑量給藥。然而，在許多臨床情況下，可能更傾向於將全日劑量單次注射給予。胺基糖苷類具有濃度依賴性殺菌作用；也就是說，增加濃度可殺死更高比例的細菌，且殺菌速度更快。此類藥物也具有顯著的抗生素後效應，即抗菌活性會持續到可測量藥物消失之後。胺基糖苷類的抗生素後效應可持續數小時。由於這些特性，相同總量的胺基糖苷類藥物以單次大劑量給予可能比多次小劑量給予更有效。當與細胞壁活性抗生素（β-內醯胺類或vancomycin）合用時，胺基糖苷類對某些細菌表現出協同殺菌作用。合併用藥的效果大於各藥物單獨使用預期的效果，也就是說，合併的殺菌效果超過加成作用。
胺基糖苷類的不良反應與時間和濃度都有關。毒性在達到某個閾值濃度之前不太可能發生，但一旦達到該濃度，超過此閾值的時間就變得關鍵。這個閾值並未精確定義，但 trough 濃度超過 2 mcg/mL 可預測毒性。在臨床相關劑量下，多次小劑量給藥時超過此閾值的總時間比單次大劑量給藥更長。多項臨床研究顯示，胺基糖苷類的單次每日劑量與多次較小劑量同樣有效——且可能毒性更低。因此，許多專家現在建議胺基糖苷類以單次每日劑量給藥。然而，每日一次給藥在治療腸球菌和葡萄球菌心內膜炎時的合併療法中的療效仍有待定義，標準的低劑量、每日三次給藥仍被推薦。相比之下，在鏈球菌心內膜炎中支持每日一次給藥的資料有限。每日一次給藥在妊娠和新生兒中的作用也未明確定義。
每日一次給藥具有潛在的實際優勢，例如，除非胺基糖苷類給藥超過3天，否則可能不需要重複測定血清濃度。一天給藥一次而非三次的藥物管理起來較不費力。而且每日一次給藥更適合門診治療。
胺基糖苷類由腎臟清除，排泄與肌酸酐清除率成正比。為避免藥物蓄積和達到毒性濃度，若腎功能受損，通常避免每日一次給藥。腎功能的快速變化（如急性腎損傷可能發生的情況）也必須監測，以避免過量或劑量不足。只要避免這些陷阱，每日一次胺基糖苷類給藥是安全有效的。若肌酸酐清除率 > 60 mL/min，則建議 gentamicin 或 tobramycin 單次每日劑量為 5-7 mg/kg（amikacin 為 15 mg/kg）。對於肌酸酐清除率 < 60 mL/min 的患者，建議採用如下所述的傳統給藥方式。使用每日一次給藥時，血清濃度通常不需要常规監測，直到治療的第2或第3天，視腎功能穩定性和預期治療持續時間而定。不需要監測 peak 濃度，因為它們會很高。目標是在給藥後18-24小時內維持 < 1 mcg/mL 的濃度。這提供了足夠的時間讓藥物 washout 發生，然後再給予下一劑。適當的 trough 濃度可通過在給藥後2小時和12小時取得的樣本測量血清濃度來準確確定，然後根據藥物的實際清除率調整劑量；或者通過在給藥後8小時取得的樣本測量濃度。若8小時濃度在 1.5 mcg/mL 和 6 mcg/mL 之間，則可在18小時達到目標 trough。
使用傳統給藥時，必須進行調整以防止腎功能不全患者藥物蓄積和毒性。要麼保持藥物劑量不變而增加給藥間隔，要麼保持間隔不變而減少劑量。已有根據血清肌酸酐水平與治療方案調整之間關係所製成的列線圖和公式。由於胺基糖苷類清除率與肌酸酐清除率成正比，確定胺基糖苷類劑量的一種方法是使用 Cockcroft-Gault 公式估算肌酸酐清除率（見第60章）。對於傳統的每日兩次或三次給藥方案，peak 血清濃度應在給藥後30-60分鐘取得血液樣本測定，trough 濃度則在下次給藥前取得樣本測定。Gentamicin 和 tobramycin 的劑量應調整以維持 peak 水平在 5-10 mcg/mL，trough 水平 < 2 mcg/mL（< 1 mcg/mL 為最佳）。
E. 不良反應 所有胺基糖苷類都具有耳毒性和腎毒性。耳毒性和腎毒性更可能發生在治療持續超過5天、使用較高劑量、老年患者以及腎功能不全的情況下。與髓袢利尿劑（如 furosemide、ethacrynic acid）或其他腎毒性藥物（如 vancomycin 或 amphotericin）併用可能增強腎毒性，應盡可能避免。耳毒性可表現為聽覺損害，初期導致耳鳴和高頻聽力損失；或表現為前庭損害，出現眩暈、動作失調和平衡喪失。腎毒性導致血清肌酸酐水平上升或肌酸酐清除率降低，儘管最早的徵兆通常是 trough 血清胺基糖苷類濃度增加。Neomycin、kanamycin 和 amikacin 是耳毒性最強的藥物。Streptomycin 和 gentamicin 是前庭毒性最強的。Neomycin、tobramycin 和 gentamicin 是腎毒性最強的。
在非常高的劑量下，胺基糖苷類可產生類似箭毒的效應，出現神經肌肉阻斷，導致呼吸麻痺。這種麻痺通常可通過 promptly 給予 calcium gluconate 或 neostigmine 逆轉。過敏反應少見。
F. 臨床應用 胺基糖苷類主要用於對抗革蘭氏陰性腸道細菌，特別是當分離株可能具有抗藥性且有敗血症懷疑時。它們幾乎總是與 β-內醯胺類抗生素併用，以擴展覆蓋範圍包括可能的革蘭氏陽性病原體，並利用這兩類藥物之間的協同作用。Penicillin-胺基糖苷類複方也用於實現腸球菌心內膜炎治療的殺菌活性，並縮短 viridans 鏈球菌和部分葡萄球菌心內膜炎患者的治療時間。使用哪種胺基糖苷類以及使用什麼劑量取決於所治療的感染和分離株的敏感性。
STREPTOMYCIN Streptomycin（圖45-1）是從一株 Streptomyces griseus 分離出來的。其抗菌活性與其他胺基糖苷類典型相同，抗藥機制也類似。抗藥性已在大多數物種中出現，嚴重限制了 streptomycin 目前的用途，以下列出的例外情況除外。對 streptomycin 的核糖體抗藥性容易產生，限制了它作為單一製劑的作用。
臨床應用 A. 分枝桿菌感染 Streptomycin 主要用作結核病治療的二線藥物。劑量為 0.5-1 g/d（兒童為 7.5-15 mg/kg/d），經肌肉注射或靜脈注射給藥。應僅與其他藥物併用以防止抗藥性的產生。關於 streptomycin 在分枝桿菌感染中使用的更多信息，見第47章。
B. 非結核性感染 在鼠疫、兔熱病，有時布氏桿菌病中，streptomycin 1 g/d（兒童為 15 mg/kg/d）經肌肉注射給藥，與口服 tetracycline 併用。
Penicillin 加上 streptomycin 對腸球菌心內膜炎和 viridans 鏈球菌心內膜炎的2週療法有效。Gentamicin 在很大程度上已取代 streptomycin 用於這些適應症。然而，streptomycin 仍是治療腸球菌感染的有用藥物，因為約15%對 gentamicin 具抗藥性的腸球菌分離株（因此對 netilmicin、tobramycin 和 amikacin 也具抗藥性）對 streptomycin 敏感。
不良反應 發燒、皮疹和其他過敏表現可能由對 streptomycin 的過敏反應引起。這最常見於長期接觸該藥物的情況，無論是接受長期療程的患者（如結核病治療）還是處理該藥物的醫護人員。偶爾脫敏會成功。
注射部位疼痛常見，但通常不嚴重。Streptomycin 最嚴重的毒性作用是前庭功能障礙——眩暈和平衡喪失。這種障礙的頻率和嚴重程度與患者年齡、血藥水平和給藥持續時間成正比。前庭功能障礙可能在血藥水平異常高的數週後（如腎功能受損的個體）或血藥水平相對較低的數月後出現。前庭毒性往往是不可逆的。Streptomycin 在妊娠期間使用可導致新生兒聾啞，因此相對禁忌。
GENTAMICIN Gentamicin 是一種從 Micromonospora purpurea 分離出的胺基糖苷類（圖45-2）。它對革蘭氏陽性和革蘭氏陰性生物都有效，許多特性與其他胺基糖苷類相似。Sisomicin 與 gentamicin 的 C1a 成分非常相似。
抗菌活性 Gentamicin sulfate 2-10 mcg/mL 可在體外抑制許多葡萄球菌、腸桿菌和其他革蘭氏陰性細菌的菌株。它單獨有效，但也可與 β-內醯胺類抗生素作為協同伴隨藥物，對 Escherichia coli、Proteus、Klebsiella pneumoniae、Enterobacter、Serratia、Stenotrophomonas 和其他可能對多種其他抗生素具有多重抗藥性的革蘭氏陰性桿菌有效。與所有胺基糖苷類一樣，它對厭氧菌沒有活性。
抗藥性 鏈球菌和腸球菌對 gentamicin 相對耐藥，這是由於藥物無法進入細胞。然而，gentamicin 與 vancomycin 或 penicillin 併用可產生強效的殺菌效果，部分原因是抑制細胞壁合成後藥物攝取增強。在單一治療期間，葡萄球菌中對 gentamicin 的抗藥性迅速出現，這是由於滲透性突變株的選擇。核糖體抗藥性罕見。在革蘭氏陰性細菌中，抗藥性最常見於質粒編碼的胺基糖苷類修飾酶。對 gentamicin 具有抗藥性的革蘭氏陰性細菌通常對 amikacin 敏感，後者對修飾酶活性更具抵抗力。修飾 gentamicin 的腸球菌酶是一種雙功能酶，也可使 amikacin、netilmicin 和 tobramycin 失活，但對 streptomycin 無效；後者由不同的酶修飾。這就是為什麼某些對 gentamicin 具有抗藥性的腸球菌對 streptomycin 敏感。
臨床應用 A. 肌肉注射或靜脈注射給藥 Gentamicin 主要用於由可能對其他藥物具有抗藥性的革蘭氏陰性細菌引起的嚴重感染（如敗血症和肺炎），尤其是 P aeruginosa、Enterobacter sp、Serratia marcescens、Proteus sp、Acinetobacter sp 和 Klebsiella sp。它通常與第二種藥物併用，因為單獨使用胺基糖苷類可能對泌尿道以外的感染無效。例如，gentamicin 不應作為單一藥物治療葡萄球菌感染，因為抗藥性會迅速出現。胺基糖苷類也不應用於肺炎的單一藥物治療，因為感染肺組織的穿透性差，局部低 pH 和低氧張力環境也有助於活性降低。Gentamicin 5-6 mg/kg/d 傳統上靜脈注射分三次等劑量給藥，但每日一次給藥對某些菌種同樣有效且毒性較低（見上文）。
Gentamicin 與細胞壁活性抗生素併用也適用於治療由革蘭氏陽性細菌（鏈球菌、葡萄球菌和腸球菌）引起的心內膜炎。合併療法實現的協同殺菌可能達到治愈所需的殺菌活性，或允許縮短治療時間。用於對抗革蘭氏陽性細菌的 gentamicin 劑量低於傳統劑量。通常藥物以 3 mg/kg/day 分三次給藥。Peak 水平應約為 3 mcg/mL，而 trough 水平應 < 1 mcg/mL。關於在治療鏈球菌心內膜炎時將 3 mg/kg 劑量作為單次每日注射的資料有限。
B. 局部和眼科給藥 含有 0.1-0.3% gentamicin sulfate 的乳膏、軟膏和溶液已被用於治療感染的燒傷、傷口或皮膚病變，以及預防靜脈導管感染。這些局部製劑對這些適應症的有效性尚不清楚。局部 gentamicin 部分被膿性滲出物滅活。可注射 10 mg subconjunctivally 用於治療眼科感染。
C. 鞘內給藥 由革蘭氏陰性細菌引起的腦膜炎已通過鞘內注射 gentamicin sulfate 1-10 mg/d 治療。然而，鞘內或腦室內 gentamicin 在新生兒腦膜炎中均無益處，而且腦室內 gentamicin 具有毒性，引起了對這種治療形式有用性的質疑。此外，可用於革蘭氏陰性腦膜炎的三代 cephalosporins 的出現已使這種療法在大多數情況下過時。
不良反應 腎毒性通常是可逆的且輕微。它發生在5-25%接受 gentamicin 超過3-5天的患者中。此類毒性至少需要調整給藥方案，並應促使重新考慮對該藥物的需求，特別是在有較低毒性替代藥物的情況下。測量 gentamicin 血清水平是必不可少的。傾向於不可逆的耳毒性主要表現為前庭功能障礙。聽力喪失也可能發生。耳毒性的發生率部分由基因決定，與粒線體 DNA 中的 point mutations 有關，在接受 gentamicin 超過5天的患者中發生率為1-5%。對 gentamicin 的過敏反應不常見。
TOBRAMYCIN 這種胺基糖苷類（圖45-2）的抗菌譜與 gentamicin 相似。雖然 gentamicin 和 tobramycin 之間有一些交叉抗藥性，但在個別菌株中是不可預測的。因此需要單獨的實驗室敏感性測試。
Tobramycin 的藥動學特性與 gentamicin 幾乎相同。Tobramycin 的每日劑量為 5-6 mg/kg，經肌肉注射或靜脈注射，傳統上分三次等劑量每8小時給藥一次。在腎功能不全時監測血藥水平是適當給藥的重要指導。
Tobramycin 的抗菌譜與 gentamicin 幾乎相同，只有少數例外。Gentamicin 對 S marcescens 略為更活躍，而 tobramycin 對 P aeruginosa 略為更活躍；Enterococcus faecalis 對 gentamicin 和 tobramycin 都敏感，但 E faecium 對 tobramycin 具抗藥性。Gentamicin 和 tobramycin 在其他方面臨床上可互換。
與其他胺基糖苷類一樣，tobramycin 具有耳毒性和腎毒性。Tobramycin 的腎毒性可能略低於 gentamicin，但差異在臨床上微不足道。Tobramycin 也以溶液（5 mL 中含 300 mg）形式配製用於吸入，治療囊狀纖維化患者複發的 P aeruginosa 下呼吸道感染。建議無論患者年齡或體重，均以 300 mg 劑量每日兩次給藥，週期為治療28天後停藥28天。吸入後1小時的血清濃度平均為 1 mcg/mL；因此，腎毒性和耳毒性很少發生。對已有腎、前庭或聽力障礙的患者使用 tobramycin 時應謹慎。
AMIKACIN Amikacin 是 kanamycin 的半合成衍生物；它比母體分子的毒性更低（圖45-2）。它對使 gentamicin 和 tobramycin 失活的許多酶具有抵抗力，因此可用於治療對後兩種藥物具有抗藥性的某些微生物。許多革蘭氏陰性細菌，包括許多 Proteus、Pseudomonas、Enterobacter 和 Serratia 的菌株，在體外被 1-20 mcg/mL 的 amikacin 抑制。肌肉注射 amikacin 500 mg 每12小時（15 mg/kg/d）後，血清 peak 水平為 10-30 mcg/mL。
對包括對 streptomycin 具抗藥性菌株在內的多重抗藥性 Mycobacterium tuberculosis 菌株通常對 amikacin 敏感。對 kanamycin 具抗藥性的菌株可能與 amikacin 有交叉抗藥性。Amikacin 用於結核病的劑量為 7.5-15 mg/kg/d，作為每日一次或每週2-3次注射，且始終與分離株敏感的其它藥物併用。
與所有胺基糖苷類一樣，amikacin 具有腎毒性和耳毒性���尤其是第八對腦神經的聽覺部分）。應監測血清濃度。對於每12小時給藥方案，目標 peak 血清濃度為 20-40 mcg/mL，trough 應維持在 4-8 mcg/mL。
NETILMICIN Netilmicin 與 gentamicin 和 tobramycin 有許多共同特點。然而，在2-去氧鏈黴胺環（環II，圖45-2）的1-氨基位置添加乙基基團，從立體上保護 netilmicin 分子免受3-氨基（環II）和2-羥基（環III）位置的酶解。因此，netilmicin 可能對某些 gentamicin 和 tobramycin 具抗藥性的細菌有效。
劑量（5-7 mg/kg/d）和給藥途徑與 gentamicin 相同。Netilmicin 在很大程度上可與 gentamicin 或 tobramycin 互換，但在美國已不再供應。
NEOMYCIN 與 KANAMYCIN Neomycin 和 kanamycin 密切相關。Paromomycin 也是該組的成員。所有藥物都有相似的特性。
抗菌活性與抗藥性 Neomycin 組的藥物對革蘭氏陽性和革蘭氏陰性細菌以及一些分枝桿菌有活性。P aeruginosa 和鏈球菌通常具有抗藥性。抗菌作用和抗藥性機制與其他胺基糖苷類相同。在選擇性腸道手術準備中廣泛使用這些藥物已導致抗藥性生物體的選擇和一些醫院內腸結腸炎的爆發。Kanamycin 和 neomycin 之間的交叉抗藥性是完全的。
藥動學 Neomycin 組的藥物從胃腸道吸收很差。口服給藥後，腸道菌群被抑制或改變，藥物經糞便排泄。任何吸收藥物的排泄主要由腎絲球過濾進入尿液。
臨床應用 Neomycin 和 kanamycin 現在僅限於局部和口服使用。Neomycin 的毒性太大，不適合腸胃外使用。隨著更強效且毒性更低的胺基糖苷類的出現，kanamycin 的腸胃外給藥也基本被放棄。Paromomycin 最近已被證明在腸胃外給藥時對內臟利什曼病有效（見第52章），這種嚴重感染可能代表這種藥物的一個重要的新用途。
A. 局部給藥 含有 1-5 mg/mL 的溶液用於感染表面或注入關節、胸腔、組織間隙或膿腔。用這種方式給藥的藥物總量必須限制在 15 mg/kg/d，因為在較高劑量下，吸收的足夠藥物可能產生全身毒性。局部應用於活動性感染是否對適當的全身治療有額外幫助值得懷疑。軟膏，通常配製為 neomycin-polymyxin-bacitracin 複方，可用於感染的皮膚病變或鼻孔以抑制葡萄球菌，但它們在很大程度上無效。
B. 口服給藥 在選擇性腸道手術準備中，口服 neomycin 1 g 每6-8小時一次，持續1-2天，通常與 1 g erythromycin base 併用。這減少了需氧腸道菌群，對厭氧菌影響很小。在肝性腦病中，通過每6-8小時給予 1 g 配合減少蛋白質攝入來抑制腸桿菌菌群，從而減少氨的產生。Neomycin 用於肝性腦病已在很大程度上被 lactulose 和其他毒性較低的藥物取代。Paromomycin 在治療原蟲感染中的使用在第52章討論。
不良反應 Neomycin 組的所有成員都具有顯著的腎毒性和耳毒性。聽覺功能受影響比前庭功能更大。聽力喪失有發生，特別是腎功能受損且藥物水平長期升高的成人。術後從腹腔吸收的 kanamycin（3-5 g）突然吸收可導致類似箭毒的神經肌肉阻斷和呼吸驟停。Calcium gluconate 和 neostigmine 可作為解毒劑。
雖然過敏不常見，但長期將含 neomycin 的軟膏應用於皮膚和眼睛已導致嚴重的過敏反應。
SPECTINOMYCIN Spectinomycin 是一種氨基環醇類抗生素，結構上與胺基糖苷類相關。它缺乏氨基糖和糖苷鍵。

Spectinomycin 在體外對許多革蘭氏陽性和革蘭氏陰性生物有活性，但它幾乎僅用作抗藥性淋病或對 penicillin 過敏患者淋病的替代治療。大多数淋球菌分離株被 6 mcg/mL 的 spectinomycin 抑制。淋球菌菌株可能對 spectinomycin 具有抗藥性，但與其他用於淋病的藥物沒有交叉抗藥性。Spectinomycin 肌肉注射後迅速吸收。單次劑量為 40 mg/kg，最高達 2 g。注射部位���痛，偶有發燒和噁心。腎毒性和貧血罕見。Spectinomycin 在美國已不再供臨床使用，但可能在其他地方有供應。
